definition_zh: 软骨；软骨组织；（食用肉中的）脆骨
definition_en: a firm but flexible connective tissue that is softer than bone and supports, cushions or shapes parts of the body
core_image: 一块半透明的弹性垫片，夹在两根硬骨之间，受力时压扁，松手后又弹回原状
scene: 解剖课上，老师把膝关节模型掰开，露出两片骨头之间的浅色垫层： The cartilage between the bones has worn thin.
sceneCN: 这里指「关节软骨」（第 2 个义项：覆盖骨端、减少摩擦的软骨层）；句意为两块骨头之间的软骨已经磨薄。图中可辨识物件：膝关节模型、两片骨端、浅色垫层、磨损标记。

pos.zh: 软骨组织（一种结缔组织）
（身体某一处的）软骨块；脆骨

derivatives.zh: 软骨素（软骨基质中的多糖）
类软骨的；质地像软骨的

senses.title: Flexible supporting tissue
senses.titleCN: 软骨组织：比骨软而有弹性的支持组织
senses.definition: a firm but flexible connective tissue that is softer than bone and holds shape without being rigid
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚实而有弹性、比骨软、能维持形状却不僵硬的结缔组织
senses.example: Cartilage gives the nose its shape without making it rigid.
senses.exampleCN: 软骨让鼻子成形，却不使它僵硬。
senses.why: Cartilage keeps its shape with a rubbery matrix instead of mineral deposits, so it bends before it breaks.
senses.whyCN: 软骨靠橡胶状的基质而非矿物沉积维持形状，因此先弯后断。

senses.title: Joint surface cushion
senses.titleCN: 关节软骨：覆盖骨端、减少摩擦
senses.definition: the smooth layer of cartilage covering the ends of bones where they meet in a joint
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在骨端接触处、使关节面光滑的软骨层
senses.example: Running on hard pavement for years wears away the cartilage in the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 多年在硬路面上跑步会磨掉膝关节的软骨。
senses.why: Two hard surfaces grinding together would soon fail, so a soft pad between them takes the friction and spreads the load.
senses.whyCN: 两块硬面直接研磨很快就会损坏，因此中间需要一层软垫承担摩擦、分散压力。

senses.title: Airway support
senses.titleCN: 呼吸道软骨：撑开管腔的环状支架
senses.definition: rings of cartilage that keep the trachea and larger airways open
senses.definitionCN: 使气管与较大气道保持张开的软骨环
senses.example: The rings of cartilage keep the trachea from collapsing when you breathe in.
senses.exampleCN: 软骨环让气管在吸气时不致塌陷。
senses.why: Soft tissue alone would close under pressure, so stiff but bendable cartilage acts as a permanent frame.
senses.whyCN: 只有软组织会在压力下闭合，因此需要坚硬又能弯曲的软骨充当常设支架。

senses.title: Elastic cartilage of ear and nose
senses.titleCN: 耳鼻的弹性软骨
senses.definition: cartilage rich in elastic fibres, found in the outer ear and the tip of the nose
senses.definitionCN: 富含弹性纤维、存在于外耳与鼻尖的软骨
senses.example: The cartilage in the ear bends easily and springs back into shape.
senses.exampleCN: 耳朵里的软骨容易弯折，又会弹回原形。
senses.why: Elastic fibres let the tissue return to its original form, which is why an ear can be folded and released.
senses.whyCN: 弹性纤维使组织能恢复原形，所以耳朵被折一下再松手还会回去。

senses.title: Cartilaginous skeleton
senses.titleCN: 软骨骨架：以软骨代替骨的支撑系统
senses.definition: a skeleton made mainly of cartilage rather than bone, as in sharks and rays
senses.definitionCN: 主要由软骨而非硬骨构成、见于鲨鱼与鳐鱼的骨架
senses.example: Sharks have a skeleton made mostly of cartilage rather than bone.
senses.exampleCN: 鲨鱼的骨架主要由软骨构成，而不是硬骨。
senses.why: The same flexible material that cushions a joint can also serve as the whole frame of an animal that needs to be light and mobile.
senses.whyCN: 用于缓冲关节的柔韧材料，也能整体充当骨架，适合需要轻便灵活的动物。

senses.title: Costal cartilage
senses.titleCN: 肋软骨：把肋骨连到胸骨
senses.definition: the bars of cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum and allow the chest to move
senses.definitionCN: 把肋骨连接到胸骨、使胸廓能够活动的软骨条
senses.example: Costal cartilage joins each rib to the sternum and flexes with every breath.
senses.exampleCN: 肋软骨把每根肋骨连到胸骨，并随呼吸弯动。
senses.why: A rigid joint would lock the ribcage, so cartilage supplies connection with just enough give for breathing.
senses.whyCN: 完全刚性的连接会锁住胸廓，因此用软骨连接，既连住又留有呼吸所需的余量。

senses.title: Avascular tissue that heals slowly
senses.titleCN: 无血管、修复缓慢的组织特性
senses.definition: cartilage contains no blood vessels, so damage to it repairs very slowly or not at all
senses.definitionCN: 软骨内部没有血管，因此受损后修复极慢，甚至不修复
senses.example: Because cartilage has no blood vessels, a torn joint surface heals very slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 由于软骨没有血管，撕裂的关节面修复得非常慢。
senses.why: Repair needs a blood supply to bring cells and material, and cartilage has none, which is why the cushion often stays worn.
senses.whyCN: 修复需要血液带来细胞与材料，而软骨没有血管，所以那层垫子常常一直磨损着。

senses.title: Gristle in food
senses.titleCN: 食用肉中的脆骨
senses.definition: the tough cartilage left in meat, hard to chew and usually trimmed away
senses.definitionCN: 留在肉里、难嚼、通常被剔除的坚韧软骨
senses.example: He cut away the cartilage before serving the chicken.
senses.exampleCN: 上鸡肉之前，他把脆骨剔掉了。
senses.why: This is the same tissue seen from the kitchen rather than the clinic: what supports a joint in the animal is simply tough gristle on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一组织在厨房而非诊室里的样子：支撑动物关节的东西，到了盘子里就是难嚼的脆骨。

intro.en: Cartilage comes through French from Latin cartilago, the anatomical word for gristle. The Latin noun is well attested, but its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cartilage 经法语来自拉丁语 cartilago，即「软骨、脆骨」的解剖用词。这个拉丁名词本身有充分书证，但其更深来源尚无定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin cartilago (genitive cartilaginis) meant gristle or cartilage and was already used by Roman medical writers for the flexible parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cartilago（属格 cartilaginis）意为「软骨、脆骨」，罗马医学作者已用它指身体中柔韧的部分。

items.en: Source uncertain: the make-up of cartilago inside Latin cannot be demonstrated. A link to cratis wickerwork has been suggested because both describe a flexible lattice, and a link to caro flesh has also been proposed; neither is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：cartilago 在拉丁语内部如何构成无法证明。有人因「柔韧的网格」这一相似性提出它与 cratis「柳条编织物」有关，也有人提出与 caro「肉」有关，两种说法都未获证实。

items.en: Old French cartilage carried the word north, keeping the Latin medical sense rather than a everyday sense.
items.cn: 古法语 cartilage 把这个词向北传，保留的是拉丁医学义，而非日常义。

items.en: English records cartilage in the late fourteenth or early fifteenth century, in anatomical and medical writing.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末或 15 世纪初的解剖与医学文献中记录了 cartilage。

items.en: Anatomical Latin kept cartilago as the standard term and built the adjective cartilagineus, the source of English cartilaginous.
items.cn: 解剖学拉丁语以 cartilago 为标准术语，并构成形容词 cartilagineus，即英语 cartilaginous 的来源。

items.en: Nineteenth-century histology divided cartilage into hyaline, elastic and fibrous types. The exact first use of each subtype name is uncertain.
items.cn: 19 世纪组织学把软骨分为透明软骨、弹性软骨与纤维软骨三类，各亚型名称的最早使用年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to cartilage; the second holds tissues and everyday words with a related meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 cartilage 形近或音近的词；第二组是意思相关的组织名称与日常用词。

entries.definition: A case holding ammunition, or a container for ink. It ends in -ridge and shares no root with cartilage.
entries.definitionCN: 弹药筒，或墨盒。结尾是 -ridge，与 cartilage 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: The adjective of cartilage, meaning made of or relating to cartilage; it is not a separate noun.
entries.definitionCN: cartilage 的形容词，意为「软骨的、由软骨构成的」，并不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: The Greek combining form for cartilage, from chondros, used in chondrocyte and chondroitin; it is a different root from Latin cartilage.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语中表示软骨的构词成分，来自 chondros，用于 chondrocyte、chondroitin；它与拉丁语 cartilage 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: The Latin noun behind the English word, still used in anatomical Latin but not as an English everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 英语词背后的拉丁名词，仍用于解剖学拉丁语，但不是英语日常词。

entries.definition: Hard tissue strengthened by calcium minerals; cartilage is softer and has no mineralized matrix.
entries.definitionCN: 由钙质矿物强化的硬组织；软骨更软，基质没有矿化。

entries.definition: A tough band that ties bone to bone; cartilage is a supporting surface, not a connecting strap.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住的坚韧带状结构；软骨是承压表面，不是连接带。

entries.definition: A cord that attaches muscle to bone; it transmits pull rather than cushioning load.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的索状结构；它传递拉力，而不是缓冲压力。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for tough cartilage found in meat; it names the same tissue outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用语中指肉里的坚韧软骨；在非技术语境里指同一种组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin and Greek roots, real anatomical terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁与希腊词根、真实的解剖术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin cartilago is the direct source; English keeps almost the whole Latin stem, so the spelling can be rebuilt from the Latin noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cartilago 是直接来源；英语几乎保留了整个拉丁词干，因此拼写可由这个拉丁名词还原。

normal.en: Greek chondros gives the modern combining form chondro-, seen in chondrocyte and chondroitin.
normal.cn: 希腊语 chondros 提供现代构词成分 chondro-，见于 chondrocyte 与 chondroitin。

normal.en: Articular cartilage sits at the joint; costal cartilage sits at the ribs; both are named by the place they serve.
normal.cn: articular cartilage 位于关节，costal cartilage 位于肋骨，两者都按所服务的位置命名。

normal.en: Cartilage is avascular, so injuries heal slowly; this one fact explains most clinical talk about it.
normal.cn: 软骨无血管，因此损伤修复慢；这一事实解释了大多数关于它的临床讨论。

normal.en: Sharks are famous for a cartilaginous skeleton, which is why cartilage appears in zoology as well as medicine.
normal.cn: 鲨鱼以软骨骨架著称，所以 cartilage 不仅出现在医学里，也出现在动物学里。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber washer between two hard plates: it takes the grinding so the plates do not.
abstract.cn: 想象两片硬板之间垫着一个橡胶垫圈：由它承受研磨，硬板才得以保全。

abstract.en: Picture a bent ear that springs back the moment your fingers let go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被折弯的耳朵，手指一松就弹回原状。

abstract.en: Picture a soft frame that slowly hardens into bone as a child grows, leaving the joints behind as permanent pads.
abstract.cn: 想象一副柔软的支架随孩子长大逐渐硬化成骨，只在关节处留下永久的软垫。

examples.en: The surgeon removed a loose piece of cartilage from the ankle joint.
examples.cn: 外科医生从踝关节取出了一块游离的软骨。

examples.en: A diet rich in collagen supports the cartilage that cushions the knees.
examples.cn: 富含胶原蛋白的饮食有助于支撑膝关节的软骨。

examples.en: Engineers are testing a gel that may one day regrow damaged cartilage.
examples.cn: 工程师正在测试一种有朝一日能让受损软骨再生的凝胶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡他力吉」（cartilage）——卡在两块硬骨之间、用力就变形的软垫 → 软骨

root: 拉丁 cartilago（属格 cartilaginis）「软骨、脆骨」，经古法语进入英语；其拉丁语内更深来源不确定，与 cratis「柳条编织物」或 caro「肉」的联系均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material: a firm but flexible pad. It appears as tissue, as a joint surface, as airway rings, as ear and nose shape, as a whole shark skeleton, as rib connectors, as a slow-healing tissue, and finally as gristle on a plate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种材料展开：坚实而有弹性的垫层。它依次呈现为组织、关节面、气道环、耳鼻外形、整副鲨鱼骨架、肋骨连接件、愈合缓慢的组织，最后是盘中难嚼的脆骨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flexible pad that keeps two hard things apart and lets them move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块有弹性的垫层，把两件硬物隔开，又让它们能够活动。

branches.en: PAD AND SURFACE: the tissue in general, and the smooth layer that takes friction at a joint.
branches.cn: 垫层与表面：泛指这种组织，以及关节处承受摩擦的光滑层。

branches.en: CONNECTOR AND FRAME: rings that hold an airway open, bars that tie ribs to the sternum.
branches.cn: 连接与支架：把气道撑开的环，把肋骨系到胸骨的条。

branches.en: ELASTICITY: an ear that springs back, and a whole animal framed in the same soft material.
branches.cn: 弹性：会弹回的耳朵，以及整副由同种软材料构成的动物骨架。

branches.en: NO BLOOD SUPPLY: without vessels, the pad cannot rebuild itself quickly.
branches.cn: 没有血供：没有血管，这块垫子就无法快速自我修复。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN VIEW: the same tissue is simply tough gristle when it reaches a plate.
branches.cn: 厨房视角：同一种组织到了盘子里，就只是难嚼的脆骨。

intro.en: Cartilage itself is a whole Latin noun rather than a prefixed form, but its stem and the Greek equivalent build the technical vocabulary of joints and skeleton.
intro.cn: cartilage 本身是一个完整的拉丁名词，并非前缀构词；但它的词干与希腊语对应词共同构成了关节与骨架的技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin cartilago gives the adjective cartilagineus; Greek chondros supplies the modern combining form chondro-, which medical English borrowed through scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cartilago 衍生形容词 cartilagineus；希腊 chondros 提供现代构词成分 chondro-，医学英语经科学拉丁语借入。

items.example: The Latin noun already named the flexible parts of the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已用来指身体中柔韧的部分。

items.meaning: made of or relating to cartilage
items.example: The shark has a cartilaginous skeleton.
items.exampleCN: 鲨鱼具有软骨骨架。

items.example: Chondro- appears in the names of cartilage cells and fibres.
items.exampleCN: chondro- 出现在软骨细胞与纤维的名称中。

items.example: Chondrocytes sit in small spaces inside the matrix.
items.exampleCN: 软骨细胞位于基质中的小腔里。

items.meaning: a polysaccharide found in cartilage matrix
items.meaningCN: 软骨基质中的一种多糖
items.example: Chondroitin sulfate helps the matrix hold water.
items.exampleCN: 硫酸软骨素帮助基质保持水分。

items.meaning: cartilage reinforced with dense fibre bundles
items.meaningCN: 由密集纤维束加固的软骨
items.example: Fibrocartilage forms the pad inside the knee.
items.exampleCN: 纤维软骨构成膝关节内的垫层。

items.meaning: glassy, translucent cartilage of joint surfaces
items.meaningCN: 关节面上玻璃样、半透明的软骨
items.example: Hyaline cartilage covers the ends of long bones.
items.exampleCN: 透明软骨覆盖长骨的骨端。

items.meaningCN: 包在软骨外面的纤维层
items.example: The perichondrium supplies cells for new cartilage.
items.exampleCN: 软骨膜为新软骨提供细胞。

items.meaning: a piece of cartilage moved to repair another site
items.meaningCN: 移植到另一处进行修复的软骨块
items.example: The surgeon used a cartilage graft from the rib.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生使用了取自肋骨的软骨移植物。

latinEntries.structure: Greek chondros, used in Latin medical texts
latinEntries.meaningCN: 软骨；颗粒（拉丁医学文献沿用）

definition_zh: 肌肉；肌力；体力；影响力；实力
definition_en: body tissue made of fibres that can contract and produce movement, or the strength and power that such tissue gives
core_image: 一束束能自己收紧的绳索，一收紧就把相连的骨头拉动
scene: 健身房教练让学员把手贴上上臂，感受发力时那团组织的变化： He felt the muscle tighten under his hand.
sceneCN: 这里指「一块肌肉」（第 2 个义项：作为解剖单位的一块肌肉）；句意为他把手按在上臂，感到那块肌肉绷紧。

pos.zh: 肌肉；肌肉组织
力量；体力；（政治、军事上的）实力

forms.label: 形容词（肌肉的；肌肉发达的）
动词（强行挤入；使劲搬动）

derivatives.zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的

senses.title: Contractile tissue
senses.titleCN: 肌肉组织：能收缩的纤维组织
senses.definition: tissue built from fibres that shorten when stimulated and so produce movement
senses.definitionCN: 由受刺激会缩短的纤维构成、从而产生运动的组织
senses.example: Skeletal muscle is built from long fibres that shorten when a nerve signal arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼肌由长纤维构成，神经信号到达时这些纤维会缩短。
senses.why: The core of the word is not shape but action: the tissue exists to pull, and only contraction makes it useful.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心不是形状而是动作：这种组织为拉动而生，只有收缩才使它有用。

senses.title: A single muscle organ
senses.titleCN: 一块肌肉：解剖学上的独立单位
senses.definition: one named bundle of muscle tissue with its own attachments, such as the biceps
senses.definitionCN: 一束有名称、有自身附着点的肌肉组织，如肱二头肌
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the muscle that controls the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了控制肩部的那块肌肉。
senses.why: Anatomy counts bundles rather than the material, so the mass of tissue becomes a countable organ with a name.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按束计数而不按材料计数，于是整团组织变成有名字、可计数的器官。

senses.title: Smooth muscle
senses.titleCN: 平滑肌：内脏壁上的不随意肌
senses.definition: the involuntary muscle found in the walls of blood vessels and internal organs
senses.definitionCN: 分布于血管壁与内脏壁、不受意志控制的肌肉
senses.example: Smooth muscle in the artery wall narrows the vessel and raises blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉壁的平滑肌使血管变窄，从而升高血压。
senses.why: The same contractile tissue works without orders from the will, so it is classified by where it sits and how it is controlled.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收缩组织可以不听意志指挥，因此按所在位置与控制方式另行分类。

senses.title: Cardiac muscle
senses.titleCN: 心肌：持续搏动的特化肌肉
senses.definition: the muscle of the heart wall, which contracts rhythmically without resting
senses.definitionCN: 心壁的肌肉，有节律地收缩且从不休息
senses.example: Cardiac muscle keeps beating without rest for a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 心肌一生都在跳动，从不休息。
senses.why: Heart muscle is a special case: it is striated like skeletal muscle but works continuously and involuntarily.
senses.whyCN: 心肌是个特例：它像骨骼肌一样有横纹，却持续工作且不受意志控制。

senses.title: Physical strength
senses.titleCN: 体力；肌力（口语用法）
senses.definition: the strength of the body, thought of as the power its muscles supply
senses.definitionCN: 身体的力量，被看作肌肉提供的力量
senses.example: It took real muscle to move the piano up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 把钢琴搬上楼确实费了不少力气。
senses.why: Strength is what muscle does, so the tissue name is used for the force itself, much as brains can stand for intelligence.
senses.whyCN: 力量是肌肉做的事，于是组织名称被用来指这种力，就像「头脑」一词可以指智力一样。

senses.title: Influence and pressure
senses.titleCN: 影响力；施压
senses.definition: power to make things happen, especially when used to push a plan through
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情办成的力量，尤指用来推动某项计划
senses.example: The mayor put muscle behind the housing plan and forced a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 市长为住房计划施加影响，推动了表决。
senses.why: Political force is imagined as bodily force: you lean on people the way a muscle leans on a load.
senses.whyCN: 政治力量被想象成身体力量：你对人施压，正如肌肉对重物施力。

senses.title: Military or economic power
senses.titleCN: 军事或经济实力（展示实力）
senses.definition: visible national or corporate power, displayed to discourage rivals
senses.definitionCN: 为震慑对手而展示的国家或企业实力
senses.example: The country showed its military muscle in a large joint exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过大规模联合演习展示军事实力。
senses.why: The display is the point: the tissue is shown rather than used, and the show is meant to be seen and feared.
senses.whyCN: 展示本身就是目的：实力被亮出来而不一定真正使用，亮的目的是让人看见并忌惮。

senses.title: Muscle memory
senses.titleCN: 肌肉记忆：熟练到无需思考的动作
senses.definition: movement skills stored so deeply by practice that they feel automatic
senses.definitionCN: 经反复练习深植、几乎自动完成的动作技能
senses.example: After years of practice, the moves are stored in muscle memory.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习之后，这些动作已存入肌肉记忆。
senses.why: The body seems to remember what the mind no longer rehearses, so the tissue is credited with the memory.
senses.whyCN: 身体似乎记住了头脑不再预演的东西，于是这份记忆被归到肌肉名下。

intro.en: Muscle goes back to Latin musculus, literally little mouse, a diminutive of mus mouse. The image is usually explained as a moving bulge under the skin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscle 可追溯到拉丁语 musculus，字面义「小老鼠」，是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式。一般认为这个形象来自皮下随动作鼓动的一块。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin musculus meant both a little mouse and a muscle. Roman writers already used it for the fleshy moving parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁 musculus 既指「小老鼠」，也指「肌肉」。罗马作家已用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The common explanation is that a muscle moving under the skin looked like a mouse running beneath cloth. This is generally accepted as an image, but it is a popular explanation rather than a documented ancient statement.
items.cn: 通常的解释是：皮下活动的肌肉像一只在布下跑动的老鼠。这一形象一般被认为是来源，但它属于通行解释，并非有明文记载的古人说明。

items.en: Greek mys meant both mouse and muscle, showing that the double meaning is very old and not a Latin invention.
items.cn: 希腊语 mys 同时指老鼠与肌肉，说明这种双重含义非常古老，并非拉丁语的独创。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as PIE mus-, seen in several branches of the family; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为原始印欧语 mus-，见于语系的多个分支；这一形式是重构形式，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French muscle carried the anatomical sense into English in the fourteenth century. The spelling kept the Latin -culus stem but dropped the ending.
items.cn: 古法语 muscle 在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语。拼写保留了拉丁词干 -culus，但去掉了词尾。

items.en: The division into skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle belongs to seventeenth- to nineteenth-century physiology; the exact dates of each label are uncertain.
items.cn: 把肌肉分为骨骼肌、平滑肌与心肌，属于 17 至 19 世纪的生理学工作；各名称的准确年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound like muscle; the second holds body parts and strength words that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是与 muscle 形近或音近的词；第二组是常被用来替代它的身体部位词与力量词。

entries.definition: A sea shellfish with a dark shell. It sounds exactly like muscle but has no anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深色贝壳的海产贝类。读音与 muscle 完全相同，但没有解剖义。

entries.definition: The snout of an animal, or a device fitted over it; the ending is -le after a z sound, not -cle.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或套在其上的装置；结尾是 z 音后的 -le，而不是 -cle。

entries.definition: The adjective of muscle, meaning relating to muscle or well developed; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: muscle 的形容词，意为「肌肉的」或「肌肉发达的」，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The whole system of muscles in a body or a region, not one single muscle.
entries.definitionCN: 一个身体或一个部位的全部肌肉系统，而非单独一块肌肉。

entries.definition: A strong cord that attaches muscle to bone; it carries the pull but cannot contract itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的强韧索带；它传递拉力，但自身不能收缩。

entries.definition: A band that holds bone to bone and stabilises a joint; it does not generate movement.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住、稳定关节的带状结构；它不产生运动。

entries.definition: An older English word for a tendon, and figuratively for strength; muscle is the flesh that pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 指肌腱的古老英语词，也可比喻力量；肌肉则是拉动它的那团肉。

entries.definition: Muscular strength, especially of a heavy build; it names the power rather than the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指魁梧体格带来的肌肉力量；它指力量而非器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin diminutive, the real Greek double meaning, and real medical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁指小形式、真实的希腊语双重含义，以及真实的医学术语组合。

normal.en: Latin musculus is a diminutive of mus mouse, and Greek mys has the same double meaning of mouse and muscle.
normal.cn: 拉丁 musculus 是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，希腊 mys 也有老鼠与肌肉的双重含义。

normal.en: The adjective is muscular and the collective noun is musculature; neither is a plural of muscle.
normal.cn: 形容词是 muscular，集合名词是 musculature；两者都不是 muscle 的复数。

normal.en: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, smooth muscle is involuntary, cardiac muscle is involuntary and rhythmic.
normal.cn: 骨骼肌受意志控制，平滑肌不受控制，心肌不受控制而有节律。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the meanings: muscle mass and muscle fiber are tissue; muscle memory and show muscle are figurative.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分了词义：muscle mass 与 muscle fiber 指组织；muscle memory 与 show muscle 是比喻。

normal.en: The same tissue is called brawn when the point is strength and sinew when the point is the cord.
normal.cn: 当重点在力量时同一组织被称为 brawn，当重点在索带时则称 sinew。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that shortens by itself, and the bone tied to it must follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一根会自己缩短的绳子，被它系住的骨头只能跟着动。

abstract.en: Picture a small animal moving under a cloth: that is the old image behind the Latin name.
abstract.cn: 想象布下有一只小动物在移动：这正是那个拉丁名称背后的古老形象。

abstract.en: Picture influence as a hand pressing on a door: political muscle is the same gesture without a body.
abstract.cn: 想象影响力是一只压住门的手：政治实力就是同一个动作，只是不再有身体。

examples.en: Regular training increases both muscle mass and muscle strength.
examples.cn: 规律训练既能增加肌肉量，也能提高肌力。

examples.en: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that drives every breath.
examples.cn: 膈是一层肌肉，驱动每一次呼吸。

examples.en: The company flexed its financial muscle to buy out its rival.
examples.cn: 这家公司展示财力，收购了对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜」（muscle）——马拉车靠的是一束束能收紧的绳索 → 肌肉

root: 拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式；一般认为皮下鼓动的肌肉被比作布下跑动的老鼠。希腊语 mys 兼指老鼠与肌肉，祖词为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one action: fibres shorten and pull. The action is then named as tissue, as a single organ, as three tissue types, as bodily force, as social pressure, as national power, and finally as memory stored in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个动作上：纤维缩短并拉动。这个动作依次被命名为组织、单块器官、三种组织类型、身体力量、社会压力、国家实力，最后是储存在动作里的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bundles of rope that shorten on command and drag whatever they are tied to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束束听令缩短的绳索，把系住的东西拖着走。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND UNIT: the tissue as material, and one named bundle as an organ.
branches.cn: 材料与单位：作为材料的组织，以及作为器官的一块有名称的肌束。

branches.en: CONTROL TYPES: smooth muscle works unseen, cardiac muscle works without pause.
branches.cn: 控制类型：平滑肌在暗处工作，心肌不停歇地工作。

branches.en: SKILL AND FORCE: strength that moves a piano, and skill that moves without thought.
branches.cn: 力量与技能：能搬动钢琴的力气，以及不经思考就能完成的技能。

branches.en: SHOWN POWER: strength displayed to deter rivals.
branches.cn: 向外展示的力量：为震慑对手而摆出的实力。

branches.en: The bridge between body and politics: the same verb put muscle behind works for both.
branches.cn: 身体与政治的桥梁：同一个搭配 put muscle behind 对两者都适用。

intro.en: Muscle is a Latin diminutive, so its ending -culus is a suffix of smallness rather than a meaningful root; the modern family grows from the stem muscul-.
intro.cn: muscle 是拉丁指小词，结尾 -culus 是表示「小」的后缀而非有实义的词根；现代词族由词干 muscul- 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin musculus and its root mus give the English family muscular, musculature and muscularity; the Greek doublet mys explains why the same image appears in both languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musculus 及其词根 mus 衍生英语的 muscular、musculature、muscularity；希腊语中的对应词 mys 说明两种语言为何出现同一形象。

items.example: The root is the ordinary Latin word for a mouse.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是拉丁语中表示老鼠的普通名词。

items.example: Musculus is literally a little mouse.
items.exampleCN: musculus 字面就是「小老鼠」。

items.example: Latin anatomy named the moving flesh musculus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学把会鼓动的肉称为 musculus。

items.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful musculature.
items.exampleCN: 这名运动员肌肉系统强健。

items.example: Judges score muscularity as well as leanness.
items.exampleCN: 裁判既看精瘦程度，也看肌肉发达程度。

items.meaning: a heavily built man, often hired as a guard or thug
items.meaningCN: 体格魁梧的男子，常受雇充当打手
items.example: Two musclemen stood at the door.
items.exampleCN: 两个壮汉站在门口。

items.meaning: relating to the link between nerves and muscles
items.meaningCN: 与神经和肌肉连接有关的
items.example: The neuromuscular junction passes the signal across.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉接头把信号传递过去。

items.meaning: inside a muscle, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 肌肉内部的，如肌肉注射
items.example: The vaccine was given by an intramuscular injection.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗通过肌肉注射给药。

definition_zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的；强硬的
definition_en: relating to muscles, or having well-developed muscles and great physical or forceful power
core_image: 手臂一弯，皮下那束绳索绷起来，轮廓清楚地顶出皮肤
scene: 泳池边，刚上岸的游泳运动员甩了甩水，背部的线条随着动作起伏： The swimmer's muscular back rippled as she pulled herself out of the pool.
sceneCN: 这里指「肌肉发达的」（第 2 个义项：体格健壮、肌肉线条明显）；句意为游泳运动员从池中撑起身体时，背部发达的肌肉随动作起伏。

pos.zh: 肌肉的；与肌肉有关的
肌肉发达的；强壮的；（政策、行动）强有力的

senses.title: Relating to muscle tissue
senses.titleCN: 与肌肉组织有关的
senses.definition: concerning muscle as tissue or as an anatomical structure
senses.definitionCN: 关于作为组织或解剖结构的肌肉
senses.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals within milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉组织能在几毫秒内对神经信号作出反应。
senses.why: The suffix -ar simply turns the noun muscle into an adjective of relation, with no added meaning.
senses.whyCN: 末尾表示关系的形容词后缀只是把表示肌肉的名词变成形容词，并未增加新义。

senses.title: Well developed physique
senses.titleCN: 肌肉发达的；体格健壮的
senses.definition: having large, clearly visible muscles and a strong build
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉大而显眼、体格强壮
senses.example: Years of rowing left him lean and muscular.
senses.exampleCN: 多年划船让他精瘦而肌肉发达。
senses.why: From relating to muscle comes the descriptive sense: a body in which muscle is prominent is called muscular.
senses.whyCN: 从「与肌肉有关」引申出描述义：肌肉突出的身体就被称作「肌肉发达的」。

senses.title: Produced by muscle
senses.titleCN: 由肌肉产生的（力量、动作）
senses.definition: done or produced by the action of muscles rather than by tools or machines
senses.definitionCN: 由肌肉动作而非工具或机器完成或产生的
senses.example: The crate was moved by muscular effort alone, with no machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 这只木箱完全靠人力搬动，没有使用机械。
senses.why: This sense names the source of the force: the effort is muscular because muscle is what supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义指明力的来源：说某项努力是「肌肉用力」，是因为力由肌肉提供。

senses.title: Of the muscular system
senses.titleCN: 肌肉系统的（教材与解剖语境）
senses.definition: belonging to the body system formed by all the muscles working with the skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 属于由全部肌肉与骨骼共同构成的身体系统
senses.example: The muscular system works with the skeleton to produce movement.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉系统与骨骼协同产生运动。
senses.why: In anatomy the adjective marks a whole system, so a single word stands for the entire set of muscles.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学中这个形容词标记整个系统，于是一个词就代表全部肌肉。

senses.title: Muscle-wasting disease
senses.titleCN: 肌肉萎缩性疾病的（医学定语）
senses.definition: describing conditions in which muscle fibres gradually weaken and waste away
senses.definitionCN: 描述肌肉纤维逐渐衰弱、萎缩的病症
senses.example: Muscular dystrophy weakens the fibres that support the limbs.
senses.exampleCN: 肌营养不良症使支撑肢体的肌肉纤维变弱。
senses.why: Here the adjective points to what the disease attacks, so the word identifies the tissue at risk rather than a healthy build.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词指出疾病攻击的对象，因此它标识的是受损组织，而非健康体格。

senses.title: Forceful writing or argument
senses.titleCN: 强有力的（文风、论证）
senses.definition: vigorous, direct and hard to resist, said of style or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 有力、直接、难以反驳，用于描述文风或论证
senses.example: The essay makes a muscular case for public transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章为公共交通提出了强有力的论证。
senses.why: Physical power is transferred to prose: an argument that pushes hard is imagined as having muscles.
senses.whyCN: 身体力量被转到文章上：推得很猛的论证被想象为长了肌肉。

senses.title: Aggressive policy
senses.titleCN: 强硬的（政策、外交手段）
senses.definition: tough and assertive, willing to use pressure rather than persuasion
senses.definitionCN: 强硬而自信，宁用压力而非说服
senses.example: The government took a muscular approach to border control.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对边境管控采取了强硬做法。
senses.why: The metaphor is of a state flexing its muscles, so a muscular policy is one that shows force instead of arguing.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的起点是国家绷起肌肉，因此用于政策时，它指亮出力量而不靠说理。

senses.title: Demanding physical labour
senses.titleCN: 需要体力的（劳动）
senses.definition: requiring heavy bodily effort and strength
senses.definitionCN: 需要大量体力与力量的
senses.example: Farming here is muscular work, done mostly by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农活是体力活，大多靠手完成。
senses.why: Work is classified by the part of the body it uses, so a job that relies on strength is called muscular.
senses.whyCN: 工作按所使用的身体部位分类，因此靠力气干的活被称为「需要体力的」。

intro.en: Muscular is muscle plus the Latin relational suffix -aris, which English took as -ar. The word first described anatomy and only later a strong build. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscular 由 muscle 加拉丁关系后缀 -aris（英语作 -ar）构成。这个词先用于解剖描述，后来才指健壮的体格。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base is Latin musculus, a diminutive of mus mouse, used by Roman writers for the moving flesh of the body.
items.cn: 词基是拉丁 musculus，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，罗马作家用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The suffix -aris formed adjectives of relation, as in militaris and popularis; it marks belonging rather than resemblance.
items.cn: 后缀 -aris 构成表示关系的形容词，如 militaris、popularis；它标记「属于」而非「相似」。

items.en: Medical Latin used muscularis for structures made of or belonging to muscle, and the adjective passed into English anatomy.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 muscularis 指由肌肉构成或属于肌肉的结构，这一形容词随后进入英语解剖学。

items.en: English records muscular in anatomical writing; the first citation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在解剖学文献中记录了 muscular，确切的最早书证年代存疑。

items.en: The descriptive sense of a strong, well-built body developed later, when muscle became a mark of health and training.
items.cn: 指体格强壮、肌肉发达的描述义出现较晚，是在肌肉成为健康与训练标志之后。

items.en: The figurative senses of forceful argument and aggressive policy belong to nineteenth- and twentieth-century political and literary writing.
items.cn: 指有力论证与强硬政策的比喻义，属于 19 至 20 世纪的政治与文学写作。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on the same stem; the second holds adjectives that also mean strong but from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形式；第二组是同样表示强壮、但角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun that muscular describes; using it as an adjective is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: muscular 所描述的名词；把它当形容词用是常见错误。

entries.definition: The entire set of muscles, not a quality; muscular describes, musculature names the set.
entries.definitionCN: 全部肌肉的集合，不是性质；muscular 描述性质，musculature 命名集合。

entries.definition: The adverb of muscular, used of how something is done, not of what something is.
entries.definitionCN: muscular 的副词形式，说明做事方式，而非描述事物性质。

entries.definition: A shellfish whose name sounds like muscle but has nothing to do with muscle fibres.
entries.definitionCN: 一种贝类，名称读音像 muscle，却与肌肉纤维毫无关系。

entries.definition: Fit and trained for sport; it stresses performance rather than the visible size of muscles.
entries.definitionCN: 健康且受过运动训练的；强调运动表现而非肌肉的体积。

entries.definition: Big and strong in a heavy way; muscular can be lean, while brawny suggests bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 魁梧有力；muscular 可以指精瘦有肌肉，brawny 则暗示块头大。

entries.definition: Lean and tough, with visible cords; it stresses wiry strength rather than muscle mass.
entries.definitionCN: 精瘦结实、筋腱明显；强调筋劲而非肌肉量。

entries.definition: The general adjective for power of any kind; muscular is the specific bodily and figurative form.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何力量的形容词；muscular 是具体的身体义与比喻义形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real suffix, a real base noun and real medical collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的名词词基与真实的医学搭配。

normal.en: muscle + -ar: the suffix means relating to, so muscular is the adjective of muscle.
normal.cn: muscle + -ar：后缀表示「与……有关」，因此 muscular 就是 muscle 的形容词。

normal.en: Musculature is the whole set, muscularity is the quality, and muscular is the describing word.
normal.cn: musculature 指整套肌肉，muscularity 指发达程度，muscular 则是描述词。

normal.en: Muscular dystrophy is the fixed medical phrase; the adjective marks the tissue the disease attacks.
normal.cn: muscular dystrophy 是固定医学短语；形容词标记疾病所攻击的组织。

normal.en: The word repeats in muscular system, muscular strength and muscular endurance, all anatomy or training contexts.
normal.cn: 这个词反复出现在 muscular system、muscular strength、muscular endurance，都是解剖或训练语境。

normal.en: Political writing uses a muscular case or a muscular policy when force replaces argument.
normal.cn: 政治写作在用力代替说理时，用 a muscular case 或 a muscular policy。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight under the skin, drawing a clear line where there was only a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象皮下有一根绳被拉紧，在原本只有曲线的地方画出一条清晰的线。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that pushes a door open instead of knocking politely.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论证直接把门推开，而不是礼貌地敲门。

abstract.en: Picture a state rolling up its sleeve: that gesture is what a muscular policy copies.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家卷起袖子：强硬政策模仿的正是这个动作。

examples.en: Muscular endurance matters more than raw strength in long-distance swimming.
examples.cn: 在长距离游泳中，肌肉耐力比单纯的力气更重要。

examples.en: The muscular wall of the artery can narrow the channel.
examples.cn: 动脉的肌肉壁能够使管道变窄。

examples.en: His muscular prose leaves little room for doubt.
examples.cn: 他强有力的文笔几乎不留质疑的余地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜了」（muscular）——马搜过全身，看哪里肌肉最发达 → 肌肉发达的

root: muscle + 拉丁关系后缀 -aris（英语 -ar）；词基为拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，指小后缀 -culus。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from plain relation to visible build, to force, to whole system, to disease, and then out of the body into prose and policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的关系义，到可见的体格，到力量，到整个系统，到疾病，再走出身体进入文章与政策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightened cord under the skin that turns a soft outline into a hard line.
core.cn: 核心意象：皮下绷紧的绳索，把柔软的轮廓变成硬朗的线条。

branches.en: RELATION: the adjective points to tissue, then to the entire system built from it.
branches.cn: 关系：形容词先指组织，再指由该组织构成的整个系统。

branches.en: VISIBLE POWER: a body with prominent muscle, and effort supplied by muscle.
branches.cn: 可见的力量：肌肉突出的身体，以及由肌肉提供的力。

branches.en: FAILURE OF TISSUE: the same adjective marks the disease that wastes the fibres.
branches.cn: 组织的失效：同一个形容词标记使纤维萎缩的疾病。

branches.en: POWER OUTSIDE THE BODY: an argument that pushes, a policy that shows force.
branches.cn: 身体之外的力量：推得动的论证，亮出力量的政策。

branches.en: WORK CLASSIFIED BY BODY: a job is muscular when strength is the main tool.
branches.cn: 按身体分类的工作：当力气是主要工具时，这份工作就是「肌肉型」的。

intro.en: Muscular is the clearest example of the -ar suffix in this family: a noun becomes a relational adjective with no change of meaning.
intro.cn: muscular 是这一词族中 -ar 后缀最清楚的例子：名词变成关系形容词，词义不变。

latinIntro.en: Latin -alis and -aris both formed relational adjectives, and English inherited both as -al and -ar; muscular, vascular and similar follow the -aris line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -alis 与 -aris 都构成关系形容词，英语分别继承为 -al 与 -ar；muscular、vascular 等走的是 -aris 一线。

items.example: The muscle tightened under his hand.
items.exampleCN: 那块肌肉在他手下绷紧。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成描述词。

items.example: Muscular endurance improves with training.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉耐力随训练提高。

items.example: The scan measured his muscularity.
items.exampleCN: 扫描测出了他的肌肉发达程度。

items.example: He lifted the beam muscularly, without a crane.
items.exampleCN: 他靠肌肉力量抬起横梁，没有用吊车。

items.example: Her musculature showed years of climbing.
items.exampleCN: 她的肌肉系统显出多年攀爬的痕迹。

items.meaning: relating to nerves and muscles together
items.meaningCN: 神经与肌肉共同相关的
items.example: Neuromuscular signals control the hand.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉信号控制手部。

items.example: The drug is given intramuscularly.
items.exampleCN: 这种药通过肌肉注射给药。

items.meaning: a genetic condition that wastes muscle
items.meaningCN: 使肌肉萎缩的遗传性疾病
items.example: Muscular dystrophy affects the fibres of the limbs.
items.exampleCN: 肌营养不良症影响四肢的肌肉纤维。

definition_zh: 组织；纸巾；薄纸；薄织物；一连串
definition_en: a group of similar cells working together in a living body, or a thin soft paper used for wiping, wrapping or writing
core_image: 无数相同的细胞像织布一样经纬相连，织成一整片可切可染的布
scene: 显微镜下，切片被染成粉紫色，细胞排列成整齐的一片： The tissue sample showed rows of identical cells.
sceneCN: 这里指「生物组织」（第 1 个义项：由相似细胞共同构成的一片组织）；句意为显微镜下的组织样本中，细胞排成一行行相同的行列。

pos.zh: 组织（生物体中的细胞群）
纸巾；薄纸；一连串（比喻）

senses.title: Groups of cells
senses.titleCN: 生物组织：相似细胞共同构成的一片
senses.definition: a group of similar cells and their surrounding material, working together as one layer or mass
senses.definitionCN: 由相似细胞及其周围物质构成、作为一个层或一块整体发挥作用的结构
senses.example: The tissue sample showed rows of identical cells.
senses.exampleCN: 组织样本中，细胞排成一行行相同的样子。
senses.why: The word came from weaving: cells are imagined as threads crossed into one fabric, so the mass reads as a woven sheet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自织造：细胞被想象成交错的线织成一匹布，于是整团组织读作一片织物。

senses.title: Paper wipe
senses.titleCN: 面巾纸：一次性擦拭用薄纸
senses.definition: a small sheet of soft paper used for wiping the nose or face and thrown away after use
senses.definitionCN: 用于擦鼻或擦脸、用后丢弃的小张软纸
senses.example: She grabbed a tissue from the box and wiped her nose.
senses.exampleCN: 她从盒里抽了一张纸巾擦鼻子。
senses.why: Thin paper is also a light fabric-like sheet, so the same word serves the woven body and the paper in a box.
senses.whyCN: 薄纸同样是一张像织物的薄片，因此同一个词既用于身体里的织物，也用于盒中的纸。

senses.title: Wrapping paper
senses.titleCN: 包装用薄纸
senses.definition: thin soft paper used to wrap fragile objects or to line boxes
senses.definitionCN: 用于包裹易碎物件或铺垫盒子的薄软纸
senses.example: The vase was wrapped in soft tissue before packing.
senses.exampleCN: 花瓶装箱前先用软薄纸包好。
senses.why: The paper is valued for being thin and yielding, exactly the qualities that make it useful around a fragile object.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸的价值在于又薄又软，正好适合包住易碎物。

senses.title: Woven fabric, historical sense
senses.titleCN: 薄织物（历史义）
senses.definition: a light woven cloth, especially one with a fine texture, as the word was used before the paper senses
senses.definitionCN: 轻薄的织物，尤指质地细密者，是纸张义出现之前的用法
senses.example: The old account book was bound in silk tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧账簿用丝质薄织物装帧。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: tistre meant to weave, and a tissue was simply the cloth that came off the loom.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：那个古法语动词意为织，这个词原本就是织机上下来的布。

senses.title: A web of lies
senses.titleCN: 一连串；一团（谎言、猜测）
senses.definition: a connected series of statements, usually false or flimsy, woven together
senses.definitionCN: 一串彼此相连的说法，通常是虚假或站不住脚的
senses.example: The report was a tissue of guesses and half-truths.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告是一堆猜测与半真半假的说法。
senses.why: The weaving image turns abstract: separate claims are threads, and a tissue is the net they make when joined.
senses.whyCN: 织造的意象转向抽象：一条条说法是线，这个词就是它们连起来形成的网。

senses.title: Soft tissue in medicine
senses.titleCN: 软组织（医学影像语境）
senses.definition: body tissue other than bone, such as muscle, fat and connective tissue, often seen on scans
senses.definitionCN: 骨以外的身体组织，如肌肉、脂肪与结缔组织，常见于影像检查
senses.example: The scan showed damage to the soft tissue around the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示关节周围软组织受损。
senses.why: Clinicians group all the non-bony material under one label, so tissue becomes a collective term for what surrounds the skeleton.
senses.whyCN: 临床把一切非骨材料归在一个标签下，于是这个词成为骨架周围物质的集合称。

senses.title: Plant tissue
senses.titleCN: 植物组织
senses.definition: similar cells in a plant, such as the water-conducting tissue of a stem
senses.definitionCN: 植物中相似的细胞群，如茎内输水的组织
senses.example: Water moves through the tissue of the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 水通过茎的组织向上移动。
senses.why: The cellular definition does not care about the kingdom, so plants have tissues on exactly the same principle as animals.
senses.whyCN: 细胞层面的定义不分动植物界，因此植物组织与动物组织遵循完全相同的原理。

senses.title: Material for culture
senses.titleCN: 培养用组织：实验中的材料
senses.definition: a small piece of living tissue kept alive in a laboratory for study or growth
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中保持存活以供研究或生长的活体小块
senses.example: The lab grew the cells from a small piece of tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室从一小块组织里培养出了这些细胞。
senses.why: In the lab the tissue stops being a layer in a body and becomes a supply of material to be kept alive outside it.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，组织不再是身体中的一层，而变成可在体外维持的供试材料。

intro.en: Tissue comes from Old French tissu, a woven fabric, the past participle of tistre to weave, from Latin texere. The biological sense is a much later branch. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tissue 来自古法语 tissu「织物」，是 tistre「织」的过去分词，源头为拉丁 texere。生物学义是很晚才分出的支线。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin texere meant to weave, plait or construct, and its past participle textus gave the noun for a woven thing.
items.cn: 拉丁 texere 意为编织、编结、构造，其过去分词 textus 提供了指「织成之物」的名词。

items.en: Old French tistre, from the same verb, produced the past participle tissu, meaning woven cloth or fabric.
items.cn: 古法语 tistre 出自同一动词，其过去分词 tissu 意为织成的布或织物。

items.en: English borrowed tissue in the fourteenth century for a light woven cloth, especially one with a rich or fine texture.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 tissue，指轻薄织物，尤指质地讲究或细密的织物。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the cellular sense is usually traced to French anatomical writing around the 1800s, but the exact first use and the person who coined it are not firmly documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：细胞义通常追溯到 1800 年前后的法国解剖学写作，但确切的最早使用与首创者缺乏可靠记载。

items.en: Thin soft paper was called tissue from the nineteenth century, and the nose-wipe sense is a twentieth-century extension.
items.cn: 薄软纸从 19 世纪起被称为 tissue，擦鼻用纸巾义则是 20 世纪的延伸。

items.en: The phrase a tissue of lies is older than the scientific sense: it treats false statements as threads woven into a net.
items.cn: a tissue of lies 这一说法比科学义更早：它把虚假说法当作织成网的线。

note.en: The first group holds words close in spelling or sound; the second holds materials and body structures that get confused with tissue.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音接近的词；第二组是容易与 tissue 混淆的材料名与身体结构名。

entries.definition: A topic, problem or edition; it begins with i- and has no t, so it is not the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 议题、问题或期号；以 i 开头且没有 t，不是同一个词。

entries.definition: A rough struggle or fight; the vowel is short /ʌ/ and the ending is -le.
entries.definitionCN: 扭打、争执；元音是短音 /ʌ/，结尾是 -le。

entries.definition: A hanging bunch of threads used as decoration; it is a decoration, not a fabric.
entries.definitionCN: 用作装饰的一束垂穗；它是装饰物，不是织物。

entries.definition: The technical adjective meaning relating to tissue; it describes while tissue names.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「组织的」的技术形容词；它作描述，tissue 作命名。

entries.definition: A thin sheet covering a surface or lining a cavity; it is one kind of tissue, not tissue in general.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖表面或衬在腔内的薄膜；它是组织的一种，而非泛指组织。

entries.definition: A body part made of several tissues working together; an organ is built from tissues, not the other way round.
entries.definitionCN: 由多种组织共同构成的身体部位；器官由组织建成，而非相反。

entries.definition: A square used at a table, usually larger and sturdier than a tissue and often reusable.
entries.definitionCN: 餐桌上用的方巾，通常比纸巾大而结实，且常可重复使用。

entries.definition: Any woven or knitted cloth; it keeps the old literal sense that tissue has mostly lost.
entries.definitionCN: 任何机织或针织布；它保留了 tissue 大多已失去的字面义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real weaving root, the real paper collocations and the real histology terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的织造词根、真实的纸张搭配与真实的组织学术语。

normal.en: Latin texere to weave gives tissue, textile, texture and context, all built on the image of threads joined.
normal.cn: 拉丁 texere「织」衍生 tissue、textile、texture、context，全部建立在「线相连」的意象上。

normal.en: Tissue paper and a tissue in a box keep the old sense of a thin sheet, not the cellular sense.
normal.cn: tissue paper 与盒装 tissue 保留的是薄片旧义，而非细胞义。

normal.en: Soft tissue is the clinical label for everything around the skeleton that is not bone.
normal.cn: soft tissue 是临床对骨架周围一切非骨材料的统称。

normal.en: Histology is the study of tissues; the Greek histos also meant a web or loom beam.
normal.cn: histology 是研究组织的学科；希腊 histos 同样有「网、织机横梁」之义。

normal.en: A tissue of lies uses the weaving image for a connected set of false statements.
normal.cn: a tissue of lies 用织造的意象指一串彼此相连的虚假说法。

abstract.en: Picture a loom: separate threads disappear into one cloth, and the cloth can be cut anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机：一根根线消失在整匹布里，而这匹布随处可裁。

abstract.en: Picture a box of thin sheets, each used once and thrown away, beside a shelf of permanent cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒薄片，用一次就丢，旁边是一架可长期使用的布。

abstract.en: Picture a net made of claims: pull one thread and the whole story unravels.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由说法织成的网：抽掉一根线，整个故事就散了。

examples.en: The pathologist examined the tissue under a microscope.
examples.cn: 病理学家在显微镜下检查了这块组织。

examples.en: Keep a box of tissues on the desk during cold season.
examples.cn: 感冒季节在桌上放一盒纸巾。

examples.en: The whole account turned out to be a tissue of excuses.
examples.cn: 整个说法最终被证明是一堆借口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提修为」（tissue）——把细胞一提一修，织成一整片 → 组织

root: 古法语 tissu「织物」，为 tistre「织」的过去分词，源自拉丁 texere「编织、构造」；texere 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from cloth and cells: a woven sheet of cells, paper sheets for wiping and wrapping, the old cloth sense, a web of lies, soft tissue, plant tissue, and tissue kept alive in a lab.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从布与细胞出发：细胞织成的一片、擦拭与包装用的薄纸、古老的织物义、谎言织成的网、软组织、植物组织，以及实验室里维持活性的组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many threads crossing into one sheet, which can be cut, stained and examined.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多线交错成一张片，可裁、可染、可检验。

branches.en: CELLS AS CLOTH: animal tissue, plant tissue, and a piece kept alive outside a body.
branches.cn: 细胞如布：动物组织、植物组织，以及在体外维持活性的小块。

branches.en: SHEETS OF MATERIAL: wrapping paper and the older woven cloth.
branches.cn: 材料薄片：包装纸，以及更早的织造布。

branches.en: WEAVING TURNED ABSTRACT: false claims are threads joined into a net.
branches.cn: 织造转为抽象：虚假说法是被织进网里的线。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL VIEW: everything around bone gets one collective label.
branches.cn: 临床视角：骨周围的一切被归入一个集合标签。

branches.en: THE PAPER SENSE: the same word names a thin sheet used once and thrown away.
branches.cn: 纸张义：同一个词也指一次性使用后丢弃的薄纸。

intro.en: Tissue is a French past participle rather than a prefixed Latin word, but its Latin root texere is highly productive across English.
intro.cn: tissue 是法语过去分词而非带前缀的拉丁词，但其拉丁词根 texere 在英语中很有能产性。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere to weave gives textus a woven thing, textura a weaving, and contexere to weave together, the source of context.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 texere「织」衍生 textus「织成之物」、textura「织法」，以及 contexere「织在一起」，即 context 的来源。

items.example: The root image is a loom rather than a cell.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根的意象是织机，而不是细胞。

items.example: A text is literally something woven together.
items.exampleCN: 文本字面上就是被织在一起的东西。

items.structure: Old French tissu, past participle of tistre
items.meaning: woven cloth; a layer of cells
items.example: The tissue sample showed rows of identical cells.
items.exampleCN: 组织样本中细胞排成整齐的行列。

items.example: The textile industry grew around the river.
items.exampleCN: 纺织业沿这条河发展起来。

items.meaning: the feel or arrangement of a woven surface
items.meaningCN: 织物表面的手感或排列
items.example: The texture of the cloth was unusually fine.
items.exampleCN: 这块布的手感异常细密。

items.meaning: the parts woven around a passage
items.meaningCN: 把文句织在其中的周边部分
items.example: The remark only makes sense in context.
items.exampleCN: 这句话只有在上下文中才说得通。

items.example: Histology class began with a slide of skin.
items.exampleCN: 组织学课从一张皮肤切片开始。

items.example: Tissular damage slows recovery.
items.exampleCN: 组织损伤会拖慢恢复。

items.meaning: keeping cells alive outside a body
items.example: Tissue culture produced enough cells for testing.
items.exampleCN: 组织培养产生了足够检测的细胞。

definition_zh: 器官；管风琴；机构；喉舌；工具
definition_en: a part of a living body that performs a special function, or an instrument, body or publication that serves a particular purpose
core_image: 一台有专门职责的装置，嵌在更大的机器里，各自完成一道工序
scene: 医院走廊的指示牌上画着人体轮廓，每个部位旁标注它负责的功能： Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
sceneCN: 这里指「生物器官」（第 1 个义项：执行特定功能的独立身体部件）；句意为腹腔里的每个器官都有各自的分工。

pos.zh: 器官（身体中执行特定功能的部分）
管风琴；机构；机关报刊；喉舌

senses.title: Body organ
senses.titleCN: 生物器官：执行特定功能的部件
senses.definition: a part of an animal or plant body made of several tissues and carrying out a special job
senses.definitionCN: 由多种组织构成、承担特定功能的动物或植物身体部件
senses.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
senses.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官都有自己的职责。
senses.why: The oldest anatomical sense treats the body as a machine with distinct working parts, each named for its task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的解剖义把身体当作一台有明确工作部件的机器，每个部件按任务命名。

senses.title: Pipe organ
senses.titleCN: 管风琴：由多组音管构成的乐器
senses.definition: a large musical instrument in which air is forced through pipes to produce sound
senses.definitionCN: 让气流通过音管发声的大型乐器
senses.example: The cathedral organ filled the hall with sound.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂的管风琴让整个大厅充满声音。
senses.why: The instrument is a set of pipes each doing one job, so the body-part word was applied to a machine made of specialised parts.
senses.whyCN: 这件乐器是一组各司其职的音管，于是「身体部件」这个词被用到由专门部件构成的机器上。

senses.title: Government body
senses.titleCN: 政府机构；机关
senses.definition: an official institution that carries out a particular public function
senses.definitionCN: 承担某项公共职能的官方机构
senses.example: The central bank is an organ of the state, not a private company.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行是国家机关，不是私人公司。
senses.why: An institution is a working part of the state in the same way an organ is a working part of a body.
senses.whyCN: 机构是国家的执行部件，正如器官是身体的执行部件。

senses.title: Party newspaper
senses.titleCN: 机关报；喉舌
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine that speaks officially for a party, union or movement
senses.definitionCN: 代表政党、工会或运动正式发声的报纸或杂志
senses.example: The party's official organ published the speech in full.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的机关报全文刊登了这篇讲话。
senses.why: A publication becomes the mouth of an organization, so the body-part word shifts from doing work to speaking for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 出版物成为组织的嘴，于是这个身体部件词从「执行工作」转为「替整体发声」。

senses.title: Vocal organs
senses.titleCN: 发声器官
senses.definition: the parts of the body, such as the larynx and vocal cords, used to produce voice
senses.definitionCN: 喉、声带等用于产生声音的身体部件
senses.example: Damage to the vocal organs can change a singer's range.
senses.exampleCN: 发声器官受损会改变歌手的音域。
senses.why: Speech is a bodily function, so the parts that produce it are organs in the strict anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 言语是一种身体功能，产生它的部件按严格解剖义就是器官。

senses.title: Sense organ
senses.titleCN: 感觉器官
senses.definition: a structure such as the eye or ear that receives a particular kind of stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 眼、耳等接收特定刺激的结构
senses.example: The eye is a sense organ tuned to light.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛是对光敏感的感觉器官。
senses.why: Each sense has a dedicated receiver, and a dedicated working part is exactly what the word organ names.
senses.whyCN: 每种感觉都有专门的接收器，而「专门的执行部件」正是这个词所指。

senses.title: Reproductive organ
senses.titleCN: 繁殖器官（动植物）
senses.definition: a structure that produces or carries sex cells, such as the flower of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 产生或承载生殖细胞的结构，如植物的花
senses.example: The flower is the reproductive organ of the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 花是植物的繁殖器官。
senses.why: The botanical use extends the anatomical word to plants, where a flower is the dedicated part for one function.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个解剖词扩展到植物：花就是专司一项功能的部件。

senses.title: Instrument or means, archaic
senses.titleCN: 工具；手段（古义）
senses.definition: an instrument or means by which something is done, the oldest general sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 用来做某事的工具或手段，是该词最古老的泛义
senses.example: In old texts, a pen is called the organ of the writer.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老文本里，笔被称为书写者的工具。
senses.why: Greek organon meant any tool, so English once used organ for instruments in general before the body and music senses took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语这个词泛指任何工具，因此英语早期曾用它泛指器具，后来才被身体义与音乐义占据。

intro.en: Organ comes from Latin organum, borrowed from Greek organon, a tool or instrument, which is generally connected with Greek ergon work. The musical and bodily senses developed separately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organ 来自拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，一般认为与希腊 ergon「工作」有关。音乐义与身体义各自独立发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek organon meant a tool, implement or instrument, including a musical instrument and, in medical writing, a part of the body.
items.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具、器具或乐器，在医学写作中也指身体的一部分。

items.en: The usual account connects organon with ergon work, so a tool is what does work; the Indo-European root behind ergon is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 通行解释把 organon 与 ergon「工作」联系起来，即工具就是干活的东西；ergon 背后的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, engine or musical instrument, and used it in translations of Greek medical texts.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum，指器具、器械或乐器，并在翻译希腊医学文献时使用它。

items.en: The church organ gave the word its everyday musical sense in medieval English, where organ meant the instrument before it meant the body part.
items.cn: 教堂管风琴让这个词在中古英语中获得日常音乐义：在指身体部件之前，organ 先指这件乐器。

items.en: The body sense was revived through medical Latin in the sixteenth century and then spread to every part with a special function.
items.cn: 身体义在 16 世纪经医学拉丁语重新兴起，随后扩展到每一个有专门功能的部件。

items.en: The sense of an official body or newspaper developed from the older idea of an instrument or mouthpiece; the exact dates of each branch are uncertain.
items.cn: 官方机构或机关报的义项由更早的「工具、喉舌」观念发展而来；各支线确切的年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on organ; the second holds body parts and general words that are often swapped for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 organ 构成的同根形式；第二组是常与它替换的身体部件词与泛用词。

entries.definition: A specialised structure inside a cell; the suffix -elle makes it a little organ, smaller than an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞内的专门结构；后缀 -elle 使它成为「小器官」，比器官更小。

entries.definition: A whole living being, not one of its parts; the suffix -ism marks the total body.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的活体，而非其中一个部件；后缀 -ism 标记整体。

entries.definition: Relating to organs or to living things; it describes and cannot stand for the noun organ.
entries.definitionCN: 与器官或生物有关的；它是描述词，不能代替名词 organ。

entries.definition: The Latin noun behind organ, still used in historical music writing for early polyphony.
entries.definitionCN: organ 背后的拉丁名词，在音乐史写作中仍指早期复调。

entries.definition: A layer of similar cells; organs are built from several tissues, so tissue is the material and organ the working unit.
entries.definitionCN: 相似细胞构成的一层；器官由多种组织建成，因此组织是材料，器官是工作单位。

entries.definition: An organ that makes and releases a substance; it is one kind of organ, not a synonym for all organs.
entries.definitionCN: 制造并释放物质的器官；它是器官的一种，并非所有器官的同义词。

entries.definition: An arm, leg or wing; a limb is an appendage, while an organ is an internal working part.
entries.definitionCN: 臂、腿或翼；肢体是附肢，而器官是内部执行部件。

entries.definition: Any tool or means, including a musical instrument; it overlaps the oldest sense of organ but lacks the body sense.
entries.definitionCN: 任何工具或手段，包括乐器；它与 organ 最古老的义项重叠，但没有身体义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek tool-word, the real musical history and the real anatomical family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊工具词、真实的音乐史与真实的解剖词族。

normal.en: Greek organon meant tool; a body organ is the tool a body uses for a job.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具；身体器官就是身体干活用的工具。

normal.en: The musical sense came first in English: organ meant the church instrument before it meant the body part.
normal.cn: 音乐义在英语中先出现：organ 先指教堂乐器，后指身体部件。

normal.en: Organelle is a little organ inside a cell; the suffix -elle marks the smaller scale.
normal.cn: organelle 是细胞里的小器官；后缀 -elle 标记更小的尺度。

normal.en: Official organ is the fixed phrase for a party newspaper, keeping the mouthpiece image.
normal.cn: official organ 是机关报的固定说法，保留了「喉舌」的意象。

normal.en: Vital organs, sense organs and reproductive organs name the function each set performs.
normal.cn: vital organs、sense organs、reproductive organs 都按各自执行的功能命名。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every bench has one job and no bench does another's work.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每张工作台只做一道工序，绝不替别人干活。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe organ: many pipes, one instrument, each pipe responsible for one note.
abstract.cn: 想象一架管风琴：许多音管，一件乐器，每根管负责一个音。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper as a mouth: the institution speaks through it the way a body speaks through a throat.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸是一张嘴：机构通过它发声，正如身体通过喉咙发声。

examples.en: The liver is an organ that removes toxins from the blood.
examples.cn: 肝脏是从血液中清除毒素的器官。

examples.en: The organ in the church was built in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 教堂里的管风琴建于 18 世纪。

examples.en: The committee is an organ of the local government.
examples.cn: 该委员会是地方政府的一个机关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，干」（organ）——哦，干活（干）的就是器官与机构 → 器官；机构

root: 拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具、乐器」，一般认为与 ergon「工作」相关；ergon 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a part with a job: a body organ, a pipe organ, a state body, a party paper, vocal organs, sense organs, plant reproductive organs, and finally any instrument at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指「有专门职责的部件」：身体器官、管风琴、国家机关、机关报、发声器官、感觉器官、植物繁殖器官，最后泛指任何工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dedicated unit inside a larger machine, each unit doing one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：更大机器中的一个专职单元，每个单元只做一件事。

branches.en: BODY PARTS: voice, sense and reproductive parts each serve one function.
branches.cn: 身体部件：发声、感觉与繁殖部件各司一职。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a set of pipes, each with one job, becomes one musical organ.
branches.cn: 乐器：一组各司其职的音管，合成一件管风琴。

branches.en: PARTY VOICE: a newspaper speaks for a movement.
branches.cn: 党的喉舌：一份报纸替一场运动发声。

branches.en: THE OLD GENERAL SENSE: any tool or means, before the body and music senses narrowed the word.
branches.cn: 古老的泛义：在身体义与音乐义收窄词义之前，泛指任何工具或手段。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO DOMAINS: body and state are both read as machines of specialised parts.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两个领域：身体与国家都被读作由专门部件组成的机器。

intro.en: Organ is a Greek loan that entered Latin, so its family mixes Greek suffixes with Latin and modern scientific endings.
intro.cn: organ 是经拉丁语进入的希腊借词，因此其词族混合了希腊后缀、拉丁后缀与现代科学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum and Greek organikos give organic; Late Latin organizare gives organize and organization; New Latin organismus gives organism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 与希腊 organikos 衍生 organic；晚期拉丁 organizare 衍生 organize 与 organization；新拉丁 organismus 衍生 organism。

items.example: The Greek word named any instrument, including a musical one.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词泛指任何器具，包括乐器。

items.example: Latin medical texts used organum for body parts.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁医学文献用 organum 指身体部件。

items.structure: organum, shortened in French and English
items.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
items.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官各有分工。

items.meaning: relating to organs or living things
items.example: Organic matter comes from living things.
items.exampleCN: 有机物来自生物。

items.example: A single cell can be a whole organism.
items.exampleCN: 单个细胞也可以是一个完整生物体。

items.meaningCN: 组织起来的机构或安排
items.example: The organization has offices in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构在三座城市设有办事处。

items.meaning: a small specialised part of a cell
items.meaningCN: 细胞内的小型专门结构
items.example: The mitochondrion is an organelle.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体是一种细胞器。

items.meaning: a person who plays the organ
items.example: The organist practised before the service.
items.exampleCN: 管风琴师在礼拜前练习。

items.meaning: a person who gives an organ for transplant
items.example: The register lists people willing to be an organ donor.
items.exampleCN: 登记册列出愿意捐献器官的人。

definition_zh: 器官系统：由多个器官协同完成同一类功能的整体
definition_en: a group of organs that work together to carry out one major function in the body
core_image: 几台不同的机器接进同一条管线，各自加工一道工序，共同完成一件大事
scene: 体检报告上，医生在人体图上圈出心、肺与血管，说明它们连成一整套装置： The heart, lungs and vessels form one organ system.
sceneCN: 这里指「器官系统」这一整体单位（第 1 个义项：多个器官协同完成一大功能）；句意为心脏、肺与血管共同构成一个器官系统。

pos.zh: 器官系统（解剖学与生理学的基本功能单位）
（某一种）器官系统，如消化系统、循环系统

collocations.zh: 按器官系统组织的方法

senses.title: Group of cooperating organs
senses.titleCN: 器官系统整体：多个器官协同完成一大功能
senses.definition: a set of organs that cooperate on one major task, such as digestion or circulation
senses.definitionCN: 为完成一项主要任务而协同工作的一组器官，如消化或循环
senses.example: The heart, lungs and vessels form one organ system.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏、肺与血管共同构成一个器官系统。
senses.why: The compound names a level above the organ: the unit is not one part but a team of parts with a shared job.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词命名的是高于器官的一层：单位不是一个部件，而是一组共享任务的部分。

senses.title: Digestive organ system
senses.titleCN: 消化器官系统：把食物处理成可吸收的物质
senses.definition: the organs that take in food, break it down and absorb it, from mouth to intestine
senses.definitionCN: 从口到肠，负责摄入、分解并吸收食物的器官整体
senses.example: The digestive organ system turns a meal into molecules the blood can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 消化器官系统把一餐饭变成血液能运输的分子。
senses.why: A long tube plus glands works as one line of production, which is why the parts count as a single system.
senses.whyCN: 一条长管加上若干腺体构成一条生产线，因此这些部件算作一个系统。

senses.title: Circulatory organ system
senses.titleCN: 循环器官系统：把血液送往全身
senses.definition: the heart, blood vessels and blood working together to move material around the body
senses.definitionCN: 心脏、血管与血液协同把物质运往全身的整体
senses.example: The circulatory organ system links every other system to the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 循环器官系统把其余每个系统都连接到肺。
senses.why: Transport is a single job shared by pump, pipes and fluid, so the three are treated as one unit.
senses.whyCN: 运输是泵、管道与液体共同承担的一项工作，因此三者被当作一个单位。

senses.title: Respiratory organ system
senses.titleCN: 呼吸器官系统：完成气体交换
senses.definition: the airways and lungs that bring oxygen in and carbon dioxide out
senses.definitionCN: 把氧气带入、把二氧化碳排出的气道与肺
senses.example: The respiratory organ system shares a boundary with the outside air.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸器官系统与外界空气直接接触。
senses.why: The lungs are the only internal organs that meet the air, so their whole set is grouped by that exchange function.
senses.whyCN: 肺是唯一与空气直接接触的内脏，因此与它们相关的一整套按气体交换功能归类。

senses.title: Nervous organ system
senses.titleCN: 神经器官系统：协调其余系统
senses.definition: the brain, spinal cord and nerves considered as one controlling system
senses.definitionCN: 把脑、脊髓与神经视为一个控制系统的整体
senses.example: The nervous organ system tells the muscles when to move.
senses.exampleCN: 神经器官系统告诉肌肉何时运动。
senses.why: Control is its own function, so the scattered nerves are counted as one system rather than many separate parts.
senses.whyCN: 控制本身是一项功能，因此散布各处的神经被算作一个系统，而非许多独立部件。

senses.title: Endocrine organ system
senses.titleCN: 内分泌器官系统：用激素远程调节
senses.definition: the glands that release hormones into the blood to regulate other organs
senses.definitionCN: 把激素释放到血液中以调节其他器官的腺体整体
senses.example: The endocrine organ system adjusts metabolism without direct nerve contact.
senses.exampleCN: 内分泌器官系统无须神经直接接触就能调节代谢。
senses.why: Glands that share a chemical channel form a system even though they are not physically connected.
senses.whyCN: 共享同一条化学通道的腺体，即使没有物理连接，也构成一个系统。

senses.title: Systems-based teaching
senses.titleCN: 按器官系统组织的医学课程
senses.definition: a way of teaching medicine in which each organ system is studied as a block
senses.definitionCN: 以每个器官系统为一个模块来教授医学的方式
senses.example: The new curriculum is organised by organ system rather than by discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 新课程按器官系统而不是按学科来组织。
senses.why: The phrase becomes a label for a teaching unit, because a system is a natural block of related facts.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语成了教学单元的标签，因为一个系统天然就是一组相关事实的模块。

senses.title: Multi-organ failure
senses.titleCN: 多器官系统衰竭（临床语境）
senses.definition: the collapse of two or more organ systems in a critically ill patient
senses.definitionCN: 危重病人身上两个或更多器官系统同时崩溃
senses.example: The infection spread until it caused failure of more than one organ system.
senses.exampleCN: 感染扩散，最终导致不止一个器官系统衰竭。
senses.why: Here the unit of counting is the system, not the organ, because failure is measured by lost functions rather than damaged parts.
senses.whyCN: 这里计数的单位是系统而非器官，因为衰竭按丧失的功能衡量，而不是按受损的部件衡量。

intro.en: Organ system joins two borrowed words: organ from Greek organon through Latin organum, and system from Greek systema through Late Latin systema. The compound is a modern anatomical label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organ system 由两个借词合成：organ 经拉丁 organum 上溯希腊 organon，system 经晚期拉丁 systema 上溯希腊 systema。这个复合词是现代解剖学标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek organon meant tool or instrument, and medical writers used it for a part of the body that performs a job.
items.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具或器具，医学作者用它指身体中执行某项工作的部件。

items.en: Greek systema meant an organised whole, built from syn- together and histanai to set up; it named a body of parts arranged for one purpose.
items.cn: 希腊 systema 意为有组织的整体，由 syn-「共同」与 histanai「设立」构成，指为同一目的安排的一组部分。

items.en: Latin took organum for instrument and systema for an organised whole, and both passed into English through French and scientific writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具、systema 指有组织的整体，两者再经法语与科学写作进入英语。

items.en: The English compound organ system belongs to the vocabulary of modern anatomy and physiology, where the body is described level by level: cell, tissue, organ, system.
items.cn: 英语复合词 organ system 属于现代解剖学与生理学的词汇，身体被逐层描述：细胞、组织、器官、系统。

items.en: Scientific Latin supplied the adjective systemicus, the source of English systemic, which marks effects that spread through a whole system rather than one spot.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语提供形容词 systemicus，即英语 systemic 的来源，用来标记波及整个系统而非局部的效应。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of the compound is not firmly dated, and the number of systems listed in textbooks has changed over time.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词最早的英语书证没有确切年代，教科书所列系统的数目也随时代变化。

note.en: The first group holds the parts of the compound and its close derivatives; the second holds other ways of grouping body parts.
note.cn: 第一组是复合词的组成部分及其近亲派生词；第二组是对身体部件另行分组的说法。

entries.definition: A single working part; an organ system is a group of such parts, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 单个执行部件；器官系统是一组这样的部件，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Any organised set of parts, from a railway network to a computer; organ system is the biological case.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有组织的部分集合，从铁路网到计算机系统；器官系统是其中的生物情形。

entries.definition: Affecting the whole body rather than one place; it describes the scope of an effect, not the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 影响全身而非局部；它描述效应的范围，而不是系统本身。

entries.definition: Done according to a plan; it comes from the same root but means orderly, not bodily.
entries.definitionCN: 按计划进行的；同出这一词根，但意思是「有条理」，与身体无关。

entries.definition: In anatomy, a set of organs serving one function, as in the digestive apparatus; it is close to organ system but older in style.
entries.definitionCN: 解剖学中为同一功能服务的一组器官，如消化装置；它与器官系统相近，但语体更旧。

entries.definition: A continuous tube or route, such as the digestive tract; it names a path, not the whole group of organs.
entries.definitionCN: 连续的管道或通路，如消化道；它命名路径，而非整组器官。

entries.definition: A set of connected points; it stresses connection rather than shared function.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的一组节点；强调连接而非共同功能。

entries.definition: The entire living body, which contains all its organ systems at once.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的活体，同时包含其全部器官系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real source words, the real hierarchy of body levels and the real clinical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的来源词、真实的身体层级与真实的临床搭配。

normal.en: Organ is a tool and system is an organised whole, so an organ system is a team of tools set up for one job.
normal.cn: organ 是工具，system 是有组织的整体，因此器官系统就是为同一任务配置的一组工具。

normal.en: The body is taught in levels: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.
normal.cn: 身体按层级教授：细胞、组织、器官、器官系统、生物体。

normal.en: The eleven commonly listed systems include digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous and endocrine.
normal.cn: 通常列出的十一个系统包括消化、循环、呼吸、神经与内分泌。

normal.en: Organ system failure and multi-organ failure are the fixed clinical phrases for collapse of whole systems.
normal.cn: organ system failure 与 multi-organ failure 是描述整套系统崩溃的固定临床说法。

normal.en: Medical schools that teach by organ system use the phrase as a curriculum label, not as an anatomical object.
normal.cn: 按器官系统授课的医学院把这个短语当作课程标签，而不是解剖对象。

abstract.en: Picture an assembly line: each machine does one step, and the line finishes the product.
abstract.cn: 想象一条装配线：每台机器做一道工序，整条线完成产品。

abstract.en: Picture a power grid: many stations, one network, and a failure anywhere dims the whole city.
abstract.cn: 想象一张电网：许多站点，一个网络，任何一处故障都会让整座城市变暗。

abstract.en: Picture an orchestra: separate sections, one score, and the piece only works when all play together.
abstract.cn: 想象一支乐队：分开的声部，一份总谱，只有全体合奏乐曲才成立。

examples.en: The digestive organ system includes the mouth, stomach and intestines.
examples.cn: 消化器官系统包括口、胃与肠。

examples.en: Physiologists study how one organ system affects another.
examples.cn: 生理学家研究一个器官系统如何影响另一个。

examples.en: Shock can lead to the failure of more than one organ system.
examples.cn: 休克可能导致不止一个器官系统衰竭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「organ（工具）+ system（体系）」——把一组工具接成一套体系 → 器官系统

root: organ（拉丁 organum，源自希腊 organon「工具」）+ system（晚期拉丁 systema，源自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」）；复合词为现代解剖学术语，最早英语书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses work at the level of the team: the group itself, five named systems, the teaching block, and the clinical failure of several systems at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「团队」这一层运作：整体本身、五个具名系统、教学模块，以及临床上多个系统同时衰竭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate machines plumbed into one line, each doing a step, the line finishing one big job.
core.cn: 核心意象：几台独立的机器接进同一条管线，各自完成一步，整条线完成一件大事。

branches.en: COOPERATING TEAMS: the digestive, circulatory and respiratory examples.
branches.cn: 协同的团队：消化、循环与呼吸三个例子。

branches.en: CONTROL AND CHEMISTRY: nerves coordinate, glands regulate through blood.
branches.cn: 控制与化学：神经负责协调，腺体通过血液调节。

branches.en: THE LABEL MOVES: the same phrase names a block in a medical curriculum.
branches.cn: 标签转移：同一个短语命名医学课程中的一个模块。

branches.en: COUNTING BY FUNCTION: failure is measured in lost systems, not damaged organs.
branches.cn: 按功能计数：衰竭以丧失的系统衡量，而非受损的器官。

branches.en: THE UNIT: a set of organs that works as one team.
branches.cn: 这个单位：一组器官像一支队伍那样协同工作。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: organ and system each keep their own history, and the plural marks several systems.
intro.cn: 这个复合词结构透明：organ 与 system 各自保留自己的来历，复数形式标记多个系统。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon entered Latin as organum, and Greek systema entered Late Latin as systema; scientific Latin added systemicus and organismus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁语作 organum，希腊 systema 进入晚期拉丁语作 systema；科学拉丁语又添 systemicus 与 organismus。

items.example: Each organ has a job of its own.
items.exampleCN: 每个器官都有自己的职责。

items.structure: Late Latin systema, from Greek systema
items.example: The system links organs into one unit.
items.exampleCN: 系统把器官连成一个单位。

items.meaningCN: 协同完成一项功能的器官整体
items.example: The heart, lungs and vessels form one organ system.
items.exampleCN: 心脏、肺与血管构成一个器官系统。

items.meaning: affecting the whole system or body
items.meaningCN: 影响整个系统或全身的
items.example: The infection became systemic.
items.exampleCN: 感染扩散到了全身。

items.meaningCN: 有条理的；按计划进行的
items.example: They made a systematic review of the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 他们对证据做了系统综述。

items.example: Multi-organ failure followed the infection.
items.exampleCN: 感染之后出现了多器官衰竭。

items.example: The organism contains every organ system at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个生物体同时包含全部器官系统。

items.meaning: a small structure inside a cell
items.example: An organelle is smaller than any organ.
items.exampleCN: 细胞器比任何器官都小。

items.meaning: the study of how whole systems work
items.meaningCN: 研究整个系统如何运作的学科
items.example: System physiology compares the load on each organ system.
items.exampleCN: 系统生理学比较各器官系统的负荷。

definition_zh: 感觉的；感官的；感觉信息的
definition_en: relating to the senses, or to the organs and nerves that receive information from the world
core_image: 一排朝外的小天线，把光、声、热、压力转成身体能读的信号
scene: 婴儿第一次摸到粗糙的毛毯，手指缩了一下，脸上露出惊讶： The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
sceneCN: 这里指「感觉的、与感官有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及感觉接收与传导）；句意为婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到毛毯粗糙的质地。

pos.zh: 感觉的；与感官有关的
感觉信息的；由感官接收的

senses.title: Relating to the senses
senses.titleCN: 与感觉、感官有关的
senses.definition: concerning the senses or the process of receiving impressions through them
senses.definitionCN: 关于感觉，或关于通过感官接收印象的过程
senses.example: The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到粗糙的质地。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the channel from world to body, so it points at the receiving side rather than the thinking side.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记从外界到身体这条通道上的一切，因此指向接收端而非思考端。

senses.title: Of the sense organs
senses.titleCN: 感觉器官的
senses.definition: belonging to organs such as the eyes, ears and skin that receive stimuli
senses.definitionCN: 属于眼、耳、皮肤等接收刺激的器官
senses.example: Sensory organs line the surface of the body and open into it.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉器官分布在体表，并向体内开口。
senses.why: Organs are the hardware of feeling, so the adjective attaches to the structures that face the outside world.
senses.whyCN: 器官是感觉的硬件，因此这个形容词附着在那些朝向外部世界的结构上。

senses.title: Of sensory nerves
senses.titleCN: 感觉神经的
senses.definition: relating to the nerves that carry signals from the body toward the brain
senses.definitionCN: 与把信号从身体传向脑的神经有关的
senses.example: A sensory nerve carries the signal from the fingertip to the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号从指尖传到脊柱。
senses.why: Once the signal leaves the organ it travels on a nerve, and the same adjective follows it inward.
senses.whyCN: 信号离开器官后由神经运输，同一个形容词也随之前行。

senses.title: Sensory input
senses.titleCN: 感觉输入：进入身体的信息
senses.definition: information coming into the body through the senses, treated as data
senses.definitionCN: 通过感官进入身体、被当作数据处理的信息
senses.example: Too much sensory input can overwhelm a small child.
senses.exampleCN: 过多的感觉输入会让幼童难以承受。
senses.why: The engineering metaphor turns feeling into a stream of signals, which is why input is the usual partner of sensory.
senses.whyCN: 工程比喻把感觉变成一股信号流，因此「输入」是这个形容词最常见的搭配。

senses.title: Sensory experience
senses.titleCN: 感官体验：由五种感觉组成的经历
senses.definition: an experience built from what can be seen, heard, touched, tasted or smelled
senses.definitionCN: 由视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉或嗅觉构成的体验
senses.example: The museum designs a sensory experience rather than a lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座博物馆设计的是感官体验，而非讲座。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes a whole event that is addressed to the body rather than to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述一整段面向身体的经历，而不是面向知识。

senses.title: Sensory evaluation of food
senses.titleCN: 食品的感官评价
senses.definition: the professional testing of food by taste, smell, appearance and texture
senses.definitionCN: 靠味、嗅、外观与质地进行的食品专业测试
senses.example: Trained panellists carry out sensory evaluation of the new bread.
senses.exampleCN: 受训的评审员对新面包进行感官评价。
senses.why: Industry uses the word because the instrument is a human sense organ, and the measurement is what the senses report.
senses.whyCN: 行业使用这个词，因为仪器就是人的感官，测量结果就是感官所报告的东西。

senses.title: Sensory processing
senses.titleCN: 感觉加工：大脑整理信号的过程
senses.definition: the way the nervous system sorts, combines and interprets signals from the senses
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统对来自感官的信号进行分类、合并与解释的方式
senses.example: Sensory processing difficulties make noise feel painful.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉加工困难会让噪声变得难以忍受。
senses.why: The focus moves from reception to handling: signals are taken in, then sorted by the brain.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从接收转到处理：信号被接收后由脑整理。

senses.title: Sensory overload or deprivation
senses.titleCN: 感觉过载与感觉剥夺
senses.definition: states in which the senses receive far too much stimulation or almost none
senses.definitionCN: 感官受到过多刺激或几乎没有刺激的状态
senses.example: Sensory deprivation in a silent room can distort time.
senses.exampleCN: 在无声房间里的感觉剥夺会扭曲时间感。
senses.why: Both extremes test the same channel, so the adjective marks conditions defined by the amount of incoming signal.
senses.whyCN: 两个极端考验的都是同一条通道，因此这个形容词标记由输入量多少来定义的状态。

intro.en: Sensory is sense plus the Latin suffix -orius, from Latin sensorius, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensory 由 sense 加拉丁后缀 -orius 构成，源头为拉丁 sensorius，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel, perceive or think, and its past participle sensus supplied the noun for feeling and the root of the whole family.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知或思考，其过去分词 sensus 提供表示感觉的名词，也是整个词族的词根。

items.en: The relational adjective sensorius meant belonging to feeling or to the seat of feeling; it survives mainly through English sensory.
items.cn: 关系形容词 sensorius 意为属于感觉或感觉中枢的，主要通过英语 sensory 留存下来。

items.en: Sense entered English through Old French sens, and the adjective sensory appears in English writing by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: sense 经古法语 sens 进入英语，形容词 sensory 在 17 世纪的英语写作中出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology split the nervous system into sensory and motor sides, fixing the modern technical use.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把神经系统分为感觉侧与运动侧，确立了现代技术用法。

items.en: Psychology extended the word to input, processing and experience, so sensory now covers far more than the organs themselves.
items.cn: 心理学把这个词扩展到输入、加工与体验，因此 sensory 现在涵盖的范围远大于器官本身。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of sensory is not firmly dated, and the earlier Medieval Latin status of sensorius is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensory 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，sensorius 在中世纪拉丁语中的使用状况也有争议。

note.en: The first group contains words built on the same root that are routinely confused; the second contains adjectives with a similar feel.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常被混淆的词；第二组是语感相近的形容词。

entries.definition: Appealing to the senses in a rich, pleasurable way; it praises the experience rather than describing the nerve pathway.
entries.definitionCN: 以丰富愉悦的方式取悦感官；它赞美体验，而非描述神经通路。

entries.definition: Relating to bodily pleasure, often sexual; it is about desire, not about sensory reception.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体快感有关，常指情欲；它讲欲望，而非感觉接收。

entries.definition: A device that detects a physical quantity; a sensor is a machine, while sensory describes a living system.
entries.definitionCN: 检测物理量的装置；sensor 是机器，sensory 描述活体系统。

entries.definition: An official who removes objectionable material; it sounds like sensor but comes from a different Latin verb meaning to assess.
entries.definitionCN: 删除不当内容的官员；读音像 sensor，但来自另一个意为「评估」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Relating to perception, the process of recognising what the senses deliver; sensory is the input, perceptual is the interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 与知觉有关的，即识别感官所给内容的过程；sensory 是输入，perceptual 是解释。

entries.definition: Relating to touch; it names one sense, while sensory covers all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 与触觉有关的；它只指一种感觉，而 sensory 涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves; sensory signals travel on neural pathways, but neural does not itself mean felt.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的；感觉信号走神经通路，但 neural 本身不表示「被感觉到」。

entries.definition: Quick to detect or react to small changes; it describes a capacity, not the whole sensory system.
entries.definitionCN: 对微小变化反应敏锐；它描述一种能力，而非整个感觉系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin participle, the real physiology split and the real industry phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁分词、真实的生理学分工与真实的行业短语。

normal.en: Sensus is the past participle of sentire to feel, so sensory means belonging to feeling.
normal.cn: sensus 是 sentire「感觉」的过去分词，因此 sensory 意为「属于感觉的」。

normal.en: Physiology pairs sensory with motor: signals come in on one side and commands go out on the other.
normal.cn: 生理学把 sensory 与 motor 配对：信号从一侧进入，指令从另一侧发出。
