normal.en: Sensory input, sensory processing and sensory overload trace a signal from door to brain to breakdown.
normal.cn: sensory input、sensory processing、sensory overload 串起信号从入口到大脑再到过载的全过程。

normal.en: Sensory evaluation is the food industry phrase for judging with eyes, nose, tongue and teeth.
normal.cn: sensory evaluation 是食品行业用语，指用眼、鼻、舌与牙齿作评判。

normal.en: The same root gives sense, sensation, sensible and sensor, so the family can be read from one stem.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor，因此整个词族可由一个词干读出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of small antennae facing outward, each tuned to one kind of weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一排朝外的小天线，每一根只对一种天气敏感。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that is also a filter: everything enters, but only some of it is let through.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门同时是过滤器：一切都来到门口，只有一部分被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a volume knob turned to maximum and then to zero; both extremes test the same channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个音量旋钮先拧到最大再拧到零：两个极端考验的是同一条通道。

examples.en: Sensory nerves carry information from the skin to the brain.
examples.cn: 感觉神经把信息从皮肤传到大脑。

examples.en: The room was designed to reduce sensory input for autistic children.
examples.cn: 这个房间的设计目的是为自闭症儿童减少感觉输入。

examples.en: A trained panel performed a sensory evaluation of the cheese.
examples.cn: 一个受训评审组对这款奶酪做了感官评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三色瑞」（sensory）——三种颜色都靠眼睛去感觉 → 感觉的；感官的

root: 拉丁 sensorius「属于感觉的」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；sentire 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run along one channel: the senses in general, the organs, the nerves, the incoming data, the experience, the professional test, the processing, and the extremes of too much or too little.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条通道展开：泛指感觉、器官、神经、输入的数据、体验、专业测试、加工过程，以及过多与过少的两个极端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: antennae facing the world, turning light, sound and pressure into readable signals.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向世界的天线，把光、声与压力转成可读的信号。

branches.en: THE ORGANS: eyes, ears and skin that face the world.
branches.cn: 这些器官：面对外部世界的眼、耳与皮肤。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL'S TRIP: nerves carry it inward, input names it as data.
branches.cn: 信号的行进：神经把它带入体内，「输入」把它命名为数据。

branches.en: TWO USES OF THE SAME WORD: a personal experience, and a professional test of a product.
branches.cn: 同一个词的两种用法：个人的体验，以及对产品的专业测试。

branches.en: THE LOAD: too much or too little stimulation breaks the system.
branches.cn: 负荷：刺激过多或过少都会让系统失灵。

branches.en: FROM WORLD TO MIND: the same adjective covers reception and the processing that follows.
branches.cn: 从世界到心智：同一个形容词既涵盖接收，也涵盖随后的加工。

intro.en: Sensory is a Latin relational adjective in -orius; the stem sens- also builds sense, sensation, sensible and sensor.
intro.cn: sensory 是带 -orius 的拉丁关系形容词；词干 sens- 还构成 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire feel gives sensus feeling and sensorius of feeling; English also borrowed sensorium, the seat of the senses, from Late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」衍生 sensus「感觉」与 sensorius「属于感觉的」；英语还从晚期拉丁语借入 sensorium「感觉中枢」。

items.example: The verb covers both bodily feeling and opinion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既指身体感觉，也指看法。

items.example: Sensus is the source of sense and sensation.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 与 sensation 的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成关系形容词。

items.example: Sensory input shapes early learning.
items.exampleCN: 感觉输入塑造早期学习。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: The sensor records temperature every minute.
items.exampleCN: 传感器每分钟记录一次温度。

items.meaning: the seat or system of the senses
items.example: The sensorium gathers signals from the whole body.
items.exampleCN: 感觉系统汇集来自全身的信号。

items.example: Sensorineural hearing loss affects the inner ear.
items.exampleCN: 感音神经性听力损失影响内耳。

items.meaning: judging a product by the senses
items.example: Sensory evaluation scored the bread on texture.
items.exampleCN: 感官评价给面包的质地打了分。

definition_zh: 感觉；知觉；轰动（事件或人）
definition_en: a physical feeling produced by the senses, or a state of great public excitement caused by something
core_image: 外界刺激撞上神经，在身体里亮起一阵可感的反应，随后传遍整群人
scene: 喝下冰水后，牙齿深处突然一阵尖锐的凉意，让人停住： A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
sceneCN: 这里指「身体感觉」（第 1 个义项：由感官刺激产生的身体感受）；句意为她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。

pos.zh: 感觉；知觉（身体上的感受）
轰动；引起轰动的人或事

derivatives.zh: 引起轰动的；耸人听闻的
耸人听闻的做法；感觉主义

senses.title: A physical feeling
senses.titleCN: 身体感觉：由刺激产生的一阵感受
senses.definition: a feeling in the body produced by something acting on the senses or on the nerves
senses.definitionCN: 由作用于感官或神经的刺激在身体中产生的感受
senses.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。
senses.why: The word names what is felt rather than what is sensed: the stimulus is outside, and the sensation is the body's response.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名「被感受到的东西」而非「被感知的对象」：刺激在外，感觉是身体的回应。

senses.title: Sensation and perception
senses.titleCN: 感觉（与知觉相对的概念）
senses.definition: the raw impression received by the senses, as studied in psychology before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中未经解释、由感官接收的原始印象
senses.example: Psychology separates sensation from perception, the meaning given to it.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学把感觉与赋予其意义的知觉区分开来。
senses.why: In this technical pair, sensation is the input before the mind labels it, which is why the two words are always taught together.
senses.whyCN: 在这一技术配对中，「感觉」是心智贴标签之前的输入，因此两个词总是成对讲授。

senses.title: A public stir
senses.titleCN: 轰动：引起众人关注的事件
senses.definition: a sudden wave of public excitement or surprise caused by an event, a person or a work
senses.definitionCN: 由事件、人物或作品引起的突然而广泛的公众激动或惊讶
senses.example: The young pianist caused a sensation at her first concert.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家在她的首场音乐会上引起轰动。
senses.why: The bodily meaning is transferred to a crowd: excitement runs through people the way a feeling runs through nerves.
senses.whyCN: 身体义被转用到人群：激动穿过众人，正如感觉穿过神经。

senses.title: A hit or a wonder
senses.titleCN: 轰动一时的人或作品
senses.definition: a person or work that becomes suddenly and widely famous
senses.definitionCN: 突然广为人知、红极一时的人或作品
senses.example: The novel was the sensation of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是当季最轰动的话题。
senses.why: The cause and the effect change places: the thing that produces the stir comes to be called the sensation itself.
senses.whyCN: 因果位置互换：引起轰动的事物本身也被称为「轰动」。

senses.title: Loss of sensation
senses.titleCN: 感觉丧失：身体某处不再有感受
senses.definition: the condition in which a part of the body can no longer feel touch, heat or pain
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部位不再能感受触、热或痛的状态
senses.example: Loss of sensation in the fingers can be a sign of nerve damage.
senses.exampleCN: 手指失去感觉可能是神经受损的迹象。
senses.why: The absence is defined against the presence: what is missing is exactly the feeling the word normally names.
senses.whyCN: 缺失是相对存在来定义的：失去的正是这个词通常所指的那种感受。

senses.title: Tactile sensation
senses.titleCN: 触觉感受
senses.definition: the feeling produced when something touches or presses on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触或压迫皮肤时产生的感受
senses.example: Tactile sensation tells the hand how rough the stone is.
senses.exampleCN: 触觉告诉手这块石头有多粗糙。
senses.why: Each sense contributes its own kind of sensation, so the word is often paired with the channel that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 每种感官贡献自己的一类感觉，因此这个词常与产生它的通道搭配。

senses.title: Physiological reception
senses.titleCN: 生理学意义上的感觉接收
senses.definition: the process by which a receptor turns a stimulus into a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 感受器把刺激转成神经信号的过程
senses.example: The study measured sensation at the level of single receptors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在单个感受器层面测量感觉。
senses.why: At this level sensation is not yet a conscious feeling but the event of conversion that makes feeling possible.
senses.whyCN: 在这一层面，感觉还不是意识到的感受，而是使感受成为可能的转换事件。

senses.title: A feeling of unease
senses.titleCN: 某种抽象感受（不安、沉重）
senses.definition: a vague emotional or bodily impression, such as a sensation of dread or of weight
senses.definitionCN: 模糊的情绪或身体印象，如不安或沉重之感
senses.example: He woke with a sensation of dread he could not explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他醒来时有一种说不出的不安感。
senses.why: The word extends from concrete feeling to any impression that seems to arrive from outside the will.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从具体感受扩展到一切仿佛不请自来的印象。

intro.en: Sensation comes from Late Latin sensatio, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel, and came into English through French. The public-stir sense is later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensation 来自晚期拉丁 sensatio，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上，经法语进入英语。轰动义出现较晚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive, and sensus named the feeling that results.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或感知，sensus 指由此产生的感受。

items.en: Late Latin sensatio named the act or state of feeling; the suffix -tio marks a process or its result.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 sensatio 指感觉的动作或状态；后缀 -tio 标记过程或其结果。

items.en: French sensation carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, first in medical and philosophical writing.
items.cn: 法语 sensation 在 17 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初见于医学与哲学写作。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century psychology fixed the pair sensation and perception as separate stages.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪心理学把 sensation 与 perception 固定为两个不同阶段。

items.en: The sense of a public sensation developed in the eighteenth century, when newspapers began to report events as waves of excitement.
items.cn: 指公众轰动的义项在 18 世纪发展起来，当时报纸开始把事件报道为一阵阵激动。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of sensation is not firmly dated, and the exact point at which the public sense separated from the medical one is unclear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensation 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，公众义从医学义中分出的确切时点也不清楚。

note.en: The first group holds same-root nouns and adjectives that are easily confused; the second holds words for related experiences.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、易混的名词与形容词；第二组是表示相近体验的词。

entries.definition: The general faculty of feeling or the meaning of a word; sensation is one specific feeling produced through it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指感觉能力或词义；sensation 是通过它产生的一次具体感受。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses; it describes the channel, while sensation names what passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官有关的；它描述通道，而 sensation 命名通过通道的东西。

entries.definition: Causing or intended to cause a stir; it is the adjective of the public sense, not of bodily feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 引起或意图引起轰动的；它是公众义的形容词，而非身体感觉的形容词。

entries.definition: A view shaped by emotion; it also comes from sentire, but through a different Latin noun, and it means opinion or feeling rather than bodily sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 受情感影响的看法；同出 sentire，但经另一个拉丁名词，意为看法或情感，而非身体感受。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for any bodily or emotional experience; sensation is its more technical or vivid counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何身体或情绪体验的日常词；sensation 是更技术或更鲜明的对应词。

entries.definition: The meaning the mind gives to what the senses deliver; sensation is the raw impression before that meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 心智赋予感官内容的意义；sensation 是意义之前的原始印象。

entries.definition: A general effect left on the mind or senses; it is vaguer and less physical than sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 留在心智或感官上的一般印象；比 sensation 更模糊、更少身体性。

entries.definition: A sudden wave of excitement; it is close to the public sense of sensation but always pleasurable.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的一阵兴奋；接近 sensation 的公众义，但总带有愉悦。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin process noun, the real psychology pair and the real newspaper phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁过程名词、真实的心理学配对与真实的报纸短语。

normal.en: Sensus is feeling, and -atio marks a process, so sensation is the event of feeling something.
normal.cn: sensus 是感觉，-atio 标记过程，因此 sensation 是「感觉到某物」这一事件。

normal.en: Psychology teaches sensation first and perception second: raw input, then meaning.
normal.cn: 心理学先讲 sensation 后讲 perception：先原始输入，后意义。

normal.en: Cause a sensation is the fixed newspaper phrase for a public stir.
normal.cn: cause a sensation 是报纸上表示「引起轰动」的固定说法。

normal.en: Loss of sensation is the clinical phrase for numbness or nerve damage.
normal.cn: loss of sensation 是表示麻木或神经损伤的临床说法。

normal.en: The adjective splits in two: sensory for the channel, sensational for the stir.
normal.cn: 形容词分成两条：sensory 指通道，sensational 指轰动。

abstract.en: Picture a struck bell: the blow is outside, the ring is inside the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一口被敲响的钟：敲击在外，余音在身体里。

abstract.en: Picture a wave crossing a crowd: one person feels it, then everyone feels it.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵波穿过人群：先是一个人感到，然后所有人都感到。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that can also be off: numbness is the same circuit with no current.
abstract.cn: 想象一个也能关闭的开关：麻木就是同一条电路断了电流。

examples.en: A burning sensation in the chest should be checked by a doctor.
examples.cn: 胸部灼热感应当请医生检查。

examples.en: The invention caused a sensation at the 1900 world fair.
examples.cn: 这项发明在 1900 年世界博览会上引起轰动。

examples.en: The drug reduces sensation in the skin before surgery.
examples.cn: 这种药在手术前降低皮肤的感觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三筛神」（sensation）——三层筛选后，神经感到的那一下 → 感觉；轰动

root: 晚期拉丁 sensatio「感觉（过程或状态）」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a single bodily feeling to the psychological concept, then out into public excitement, a famous work, numbness, touch, receptor-level reception, and finally a vague impression of dread.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一次身体感受出发，到心理学概念，再走向公众轰动、成名作品、麻木、触觉、感受器层面的接收，最后是模糊的不安印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stimulus strikes a nerve and a felt response lights up inside the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：刺激撞上神经，身体内部亮起一阵可感的回应。

branches.en: LOSS AND TOUCH: feeling can vanish, and one channel still delivers it.
branches.cn: 丧失与触觉：感觉会消失，而某个通道仍能传递它。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL LADDER: the psychological input and the receptor event beneath it.
branches.cn: 技术阶梯：心理学的输入概念，以及其下感受器层面的事件。

branches.en: THE WONDER: the thing itself becomes famous overnight.
branches.cn: 轰动之物：那件事物本身一夜之间人尽皆知。

branches.en: VAGUE IMPRESSION: a feeling that arrives without a clear source.
branches.cn: 模糊印象：没有明确来源却出现的感受。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO SCALES: nerves and crowds both conduct a wave of feeling.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两种尺度：神经与人群都在传导一阵感受。

intro.en: Sensation is a Latin process noun: the stem sens- plus -ation, the English form of Latin -tio.
intro.cn: sensation 是拉丁过程名词：词干 sens- 加 -ation，即拉丁 -tio 的英语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire gives sensus and sensatio; the adjective sensualis and the noun sentimentum belong to neighbouring branches of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 衍生 sensus 与 sensatio；形容词 sensualis 与名词 sentimentum 属于同一词族的邻近支线。

items.example: The whole family rests on this verb.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都建立在这个动词上。

items.example: Sensus is the noun behind sense.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: Sensory nerves carry the signal inward.
items.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号向体内传导。

items.example: The result was sensational.
items.exampleCN: 结果引起轰动。

items.example: The paper was accused of sensationalism.
items.exampleCN: 这家报纸被指刻意耸人听闻。

items.meaning: able to be felt; also reasonable
items.example: The difference was barely sensible.
items.exampleCN: 这点差别几乎感觉不到。

items.example: The scarred skin was insensitive to touch.
items.exampleCN: 留疤的皮肤对触摸不敏感。

definition_zh: 感觉器官：专门接收某类刺激并转成神经信号的结构
definition_en: a body structure specialised for receiving one kind of stimulus and turning it into a nerve signal
core_image: 一排各自朝向一种信号的接收器：眼对光、耳对声、舌对味
scene: 生物课上，老师让学生依次遮住眼、捂住耳，体会信息从哪里进入身体： Each sensory organ responds to only one kind of stimulus.
sceneCN: 这里指「感觉器官」这一整体类别（第 1 个义项：专门接收某类刺激的结构）；句意为每个感觉器官只对一类刺激作出反应。

pos.zh: 感觉器官（解剖学与生理学的基本结构）
（某一种）感觉器官，如眼、耳、鼻、舌

senses.title: Organ built for one kind of stimulus
senses.titleCN: 感觉器官总称：专为某类刺激而生的结构
senses.definition: a structure in the body that is specialised to detect one kind of stimulus and send a signal to the nervous system
senses.definitionCN: 身体中专为检测某一类刺激并向神经系统发送信号的结构
senses.example: Each sensory organ responds to only one kind of stimulus.
senses.exampleCN: 每个感觉器官只对一类刺激作出反应。
senses.why: The name states both halves: sensory for the channel, organ for a dedicated working part. Together they mark a structure built for one signal.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称把两半都说清楚：前半指通道，后半指专职部件。合起来标记为某一种信号而生的结构。

senses.title: The eye
senses.titleCN: 视觉器官：眼
senses.definition: the organ that detects light and forms an image for the visual system
senses.definitionCN: 检测光并为视觉系统形成图像的器官
senses.example: The eye is the sensory organ that turns light into signals.
senses.exampleCN: 眼是把光转成信号的感觉器官。
senses.why: Vision needs a surface that catches light and a lens that focuses it, so a whole organ is built around one physical quantity.
senses.whyCN: 视觉需要一个承接光的表面和一个聚焦的透镜，因此整个器官围绕一种物理量建成。

senses.title: The ear
senses.titleCN: 听觉器官：耳
senses.definition: the organ that detects sound waves and also helps maintain balance
senses.definitionCN: 检测声波并帮助维持平衡的器官
senses.example: The ear is a sensory organ for sound and for balance.
senses.exampleCN: 耳是感受声音与平衡的感觉器官。
senses.why: One organ serves two senses here, which is why the ear is a good counterexample to a strict one-organ-one-sense rule.
senses.whyCN: 同一个器官在这里服务两种感觉，这正是耳对「一器官一感觉」这一严格规则的好反例。

senses.title: The nose
senses.titleCN: 嗅觉器官：鼻
senses.definition: the organ that detects airborne molecules and produces smell
senses.definitionCN: 检测空气中分子并产生嗅觉的器官
senses.example: The nose is the sensory organ that detects molecules in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 鼻是检测空气中分子的感觉器官。
senses.why: Smell requires a moist surface exposed to air, so the organ is shaped as a cavity rather than a flat patch.
senses.whyCN: 嗅觉需要一个暴露于空气的湿润表面，因此这个器官呈腔状而非平面。

senses.title: The tongue
senses.titleCN: 味觉器官：舌
senses.definition: the organ that detects dissolved substances and produces taste
senses.definitionCN: 检测溶解物质并产生味觉的器官
senses.example: The tongue is the sensory organ for dissolved flavours.
senses.exampleCN: 舌是感受溶解风味的器官。
senses.why: Taste needs contact with liquid, so the organ is muscular and wet, built to move food against its surface.
senses.whyCN: 味觉需要与液体接触，因此这个器官有肌肉、表面湿润，专门把食物推到其上。

senses.title: The skin
senses.titleCN: 触觉器官：皮肤
senses.definition: the body covering that detects touch, pressure, heat and cold
senses.definitionCN: 检测触、压、热与冷的身体覆盖层
senses.example: The skin is a sensory organ spread over the whole body.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤是铺展于全身的感觉器官。
senses.why: Touch is not localised in one small part, so the organ is the whole surface rather than a single knob.
senses.whyCN: 触觉并不集中在一小块，因此这个器官是整片表面而非单个凸起。

senses.title: Specialisation in evolution
senses.titleCN: 特化：演化中形成的专门结构
senses.definition: the process by which a sensory structure becomes tuned to one narrow range of signals
senses.definitionCN: 感觉结构变得只对某一狭窄信号范围敏感的过程
senses.example: In cave fish, the sensory organ for touch became more elaborate as the eyes shrank.
senses.exampleCN: 在洞穴鱼中，随着眼睛退化，触觉感觉器官变得更复杂。
senses.why: When one channel closes, others may open wider, so specialisation is a story about trade-offs rather than simple addition.
senses.whyCN: 一条通道关闭时，别的通道可能张得更开，因此特化讲的是取舍而非简单叠加。

senses.title: Damage and replacement
senses.titleCN: 感觉器官损伤与功能替代
senses.definition: loss of a sensory organ and the use of implants or devices to replace its function
senses.definitionCN: 感觉器官的丧失，以及用植入物或装置替代其功能
senses.example: A cochlear implant replaces part of the function of a damaged sensory organ.
senses.exampleCN: 人工耳蜗替代了受损感觉器官的部分功能。
senses.why: Once the organ is treated as a device for one signal, engineering can imitate that function even when the tissue cannot be restored.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把器官当作处理单一信号的装置，即使组织无法恢复，工程也能模仿其功能。

intro.en: Sensory organ combines sensory, from Latin sensorius of feeling, and organ, from Greek organon a tool through Latin organum. The compound is a modern anatomical label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensory organ 由 sensory（拉丁 sensorius「属于感觉的」）与 organ（经拉丁 organum 上溯希腊 organon「工具」）合成。这个复合词是现代解剖学标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek organon meant tool or instrument, and medical writers already used it for a working part of the body.
items.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具或器具，医学作者已用它指身体中执行工作的部件。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument and for a body part, and the word reached English through French.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具与身体部件，这个词再经法语进入英语。

items.en: Sensorius meant belonging to feeling, and English sensory comes from it; the compound puts the adjective before the organ it qualifies.
items.cn: sensorius 意为属于感觉的，英语 sensory 由此而来；复合词把这个形容词放在它所修饰的器官之前。

items.en: The phrase sense organ or sensory organ became standard in anatomy and physiology, where structures are grouped by the signal they receive.
items.cn: sense organ 或 sensory organ 成为解剖学与生理学的标准说法，结构按所接收的信号归类。

items.en: Nineteenth-century comparative biology compared sensory organs across animals and introduced the idea of specialisation.
items.cn: 19 世纪比较生物学在不同动物间比较感觉器官，并提出特化概念。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of the exact compound is not firmly dated, and sense organ and sensory organ have never been fully fixed in preference.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切复合词最早的英语书证没有确定年代，sense organ 与 sensory organ 的优先用法也从未完全固定。

note.en: The first group holds the two halves of the compound and its common variant; the second holds structures and devices that are close in function.
note.cn: 第一组是复合词的两半及其常见变体；第二组是功能相近的结构与装置。

entries.definition: The older and shorter synonym; it is interchangeable in anatomy, though sensory organ is more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 更早、更短的同类说法；在解剖学中可互换，但 sensory organ 更正式。

entries.definition: The adjective half; on its own it cannot name a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的形容词一半；单独使用时不能命名结构。

entries.definition: A manufactured detector; a sensory organ is living tissue, while a sensor is built.
entries.definitionCN: 人造的检测装置；感觉器官是活组织，而 sensor 是制造出来的。

entries.definition: A structure inside a cell; it is far smaller than an organ and cannot serve a whole sense.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞内的结构；远小于器官，也不能承担一整套感觉。

entries.definition: A cell or nerve ending that detects a stimulus; many receptors together build the tissue of a sensory organ.
entries.definitionCN: 检测刺激的细胞或神经末梢；许多感受器共同构成感觉器官的组织。

entries.definition: A structure that carries out a response, such as a muscle; it is the opposite end of the sensory path.
entries.definitionCN: 执行反应的结构，如肌肉；它是感觉通路的另一端。

entries.definition: A bundle of fibres that carries signals; it connects the organ to the brain but is not the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 传导信号的纤维束；它把器官连到脑，但本身不是器官。

entries.definition: The seat or system of the senses as a whole, not one individual organ.
entries.definitionCN: 整体意义上的感觉中枢或感觉系统，而非单个器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek tool-word, the real Latin feeling adjective and the real anatomy pairing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊工具词、真实的拉丁感觉形容词与真实的解剖配对。

normal.en: Sensory supplies the channel, organ supplies the dedicated part, and together they name a structure built for one signal.
normal.cn: sensory 提供通道，organ 提供专职部件，合起来命名一个为单一信号而建的结构。

normal.en: Anatomy often writes sense organ; the two forms are synonyms with different formality.
normal.cn: 解剖学常写 sense organ；两种形式是同义词，正式程度不同。

normal.en: Each organ maps to a physical quantity: light for the eye, sound for the ear, molecules for the nose, dissolved substances for the tongue.
normal.cn: 每个器官对应一种物理量：眼对光、耳对声、鼻对分子、舌对溶解物质。

normal.en: Receptors are cells inside the organ, so receptor is smaller and sensory organ is larger.
normal.cn: 感受器是器官内部的细胞，因此 receptor 更小，sensory organ 更大。

normal.en: The ear breaks the one-organ-one-sense rule because it also handles balance.
normal.cn: 耳打破了「一器官一感觉」的规则，因为它还负责平衡。

abstract.en: Picture a bank of radio receivers, each tuned to a single frequency.
abstract.cn: 想象一排无线电接收器，每一台只调到一个频率。

abstract.en: Picture a single ear that hears and also feels which way is down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只耳朵既能听声，也能感觉哪边朝下。

abstract.en: Picture a broken receiver replaced by a small machine that imitates its job.
abstract.cn: 想象一台坏掉的接收器被一台模仿其工作的小机器替代。

examples.en: The eye is the most studied sensory organ in vertebrates.
examples.cn: 眼是脊椎动物中被研究得最多的感觉器官。

examples.en: Damage to a sensory organ can change how the brain reads the world.
examples.cn: 感觉器官受损会改变大脑读取世界的方式。

examples.en: Engineers are designing an artificial sensory organ for robots.
examples.cn: 工程师正在为机器人设计人工感觉器官。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sensory（感觉）+ organ（器官）」——专门接收感觉的那件器官 → 感觉器官

root: sensory（拉丁 sensorius「属于感觉的」）+ organ（拉丁 organum，源自希腊 organon「工具」）；整个复合词为现代解剖学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the general category and then walk through the five classic organs, the evolutionary tuning of a structure, and the clinical replacement of a lost function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先给总类，再依次走过五种经典器官、结构在演化中的调校，以及临床上对丧失功能的替代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of receivers, each facing one kind of signal and blind to the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排接收器，每个只朝向一类信号，对其余一概不察。

branches.en: THE CONTACT SENSES: nose, tongue and skin read chemistry, taste and touch.
branches.cn: 接触性感官：鼻、舌与皮肤分别读取化学、味觉与触觉。

branches.en: TWO PHYSICAL CHANNELS: light for the eye, sound and balance for the ear.
branches.cn: 两种物理通道：眼对光，耳对声与平衡。

branches.en: EVOLUTIONARY TRADE-OFF: when one channel fades, another may sharpen.
branches.cn: 演化取舍：一条通道退化时，另一条可能变得更敏锐。

branches.en: ENGINEERING MIRROR: a lost organ can be partly replaced by a device.
branches.cn: 工程镜像：丧失的器官可由装置部分替代。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: any structure built to detect one kind of signal.
branches.cn: 定义：任何为检测某一类信号而生的结构。

intro.en: The compound is fully analysable: sensory marks the channel, organ marks the working part, and the plural marks several structures.
intro.cn: 这个复合词完全可分析：sensory 标记通道，organ 标记工作部件，复数标记多个结构。

latinIntro.en: Latin sensorius and organum supply both halves; Greek organon and sensus sit behind them, and receptor adds a Latin -or agent noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sensorius 与 organum 提供两半；其背后是希腊 organon 与拉丁 sensus，而 receptor 又加了拉丁 -or 施事名词后缀。

items.example: Sensory signals enter through the skin.
items.exampleCN: 感觉信号通过皮肤进入。

items.example: The organ is built for one job.
items.exampleCN: 这个器官为一项工作而建。

items.meaning: a structure for one kind of stimulus
items.example: Each sensory organ responds to only one kind of stimulus.
items.exampleCN: 每个感觉器官只对一类刺激作出反应。

items.meaning: a cell or ending that takes in a stimulus
items.meaningCN: 接收刺激的细胞或末梢
items.example: Receptors sit inside the sensory organ.
items.exampleCN: 感受器位于感觉器官内部。

items.example: Sensorineural loss affects the inner ear.
items.exampleCN: 感音神经性损失影响内耳。

items.example: The sensorium combines signals from every organ.
items.exampleCN: 感觉系统合并来自每个器官的信号。

items.meaningCN: 为某一狭窄功能而适应
items.example: The eye is a specialised sensory organ.
items.exampleCN: 眼是特化的感觉器官。

items.meaning: a device that substitutes for hearing function
items.example: The cochlear implant restores part of the lost function.
items.exampleCN: 人工耳蜗恢复了部分丧失的功能。

items.meaning: made by art rather than nature
items.meaningCN: 人工制造的，而非自然生成
items.example: An artificial sensory organ can detect heat.
items.exampleCN: 人工感觉器官能检测热量。

definition_zh: 神经系统：由脑、脊髓与神经构成、负责控制与协调的整体
definition_en: the network of brain, spinal cord and nerves that controls and coordinates the body
core_image: 一张布满全身的电线网，中央控制室发出信号，各处立刻响应
scene: 解剖标本旁，老师用细针指着从脑向下延伸的白色线路： The nervous system carries signals from the brain to every limb.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经系统」这一整体（第 1 个义项：脑、脊髓与神经构成的协调网络）；句意为神经系统把信号从脑传到每一条肢体。

pos.zh: 神经系统（解剖学与生理学的基本系统）
（某一层次的）神经系统，如中枢神经系统、自主神经系统

senses.title: The whole network
senses.titleCN: 神经系统整体：控制与协调的网络
senses.definition: the entire set of nerve tissue, brain and spinal cord that senses, decides and commands
senses.definitionCN: 由神经组织、脑与脊髓构成、负责感知、判断与下达指令的整个系统
senses.example: The nervous system carries signals from the brain to every limb.
senses.exampleCN: 神经系统把信号从脑传到每条肢体。
senses.why: The word names a network rather than a part: what matters is the wiring that joins sensing, deciding and acting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个网络而非一个部件：关键在于把感知、判断与行动连接起来的线路。

senses.title: Central nervous system
senses.titleCN: 中枢神经系统：脑与脊髓
senses.definition: the brain and spinal cord, the part that integrates information and issues commands
senses.definitionCN: 脑与脊髓，即整合信息并发出指令的部分
senses.example: The central nervous system includes the brain and the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 中枢神经系统包括脑与脊髓。
senses.why: Some parts only carry messages while others decide, so the deciders are grouped as the centre.
senses.whyCN: 有些部位只传递消息，另一些负责决定，因此负责决定的部分被归为中心。

senses.title: Peripheral nervous system
senses.titleCN: 外周神经系统：脑与脊髓之外的神经
senses.definition: the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord that connect them to the rest of the body
senses.definitionCN: 脑与脊髓之外、把它们连接到身体其余部分的神经
senses.example: The peripheral nervous system links the skin to the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 外周神经系统把皮肤连接到脊髓。
senses.why: The geography of inside and outside the centre defines this division, not the kind of tissue.
senses.whyCN: 这一划分由「在中心之内还是之外」的地理位置决定，而非组织种类。

senses.title: Autonomic nervous system
senses.titleCN: 自主神经系统：自动调节内脏
senses.definition: the part that controls heart rate, digestion and other functions without conscious effort
senses.definitionCN: 无需有意识努力即可控制心率、消化等功能的部位
senses.example: The autonomic nervous system keeps the heart beating while you sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 自主神经系统在你睡着时仍让心脏跳动。
senses.why: Some control must run without permission, so a subsystem is named for being self-governing.
senses.whyCN: 有些控制必须在无人许可时照常运行，因此这一子系统按「自治」命名。

senses.title: Sympathetic nervous system
senses.titleCN: 交感神经系统：应激时的加速装置
senses.definition: the branch that raises heart rate and prepares the body for danger or effort
senses.definitionCN: 提高心率、让身体为危险或用力做好准备的支系
senses.example: The sympathetic nervous system floods the body with adrenaline.
senses.exampleCN: 交感神经系统让肾上腺素涌遍全身。
senses.why: The same network has a fast branch and a calm branch, and each is named for the state it produces.
senses.whyCN: 同一网络有一条加速支与一条平静支，各自按所产生的状态命名。

senses.title: Signal transmission function
senses.titleCN: 神经系统的信号传导功能
senses.definition: the function of carrying electrical and chemical signals between body parts
senses.definitionCN: 在身体各部位之间传递电信号与化学信号的功能
senses.example: The nervous system transmits a signal along the arm in milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 神经系统在几毫秒内把信号沿手臂传出去。
senses.why: The system is defined by what it carries: messages, not blood or air.
senses.whyCN: 这个系统由它所运送的东西定义：消息，而不是血液或空气。

senses.title: Disorders of the system
senses.titleCN: 神经系统疾病与损伤
senses.definition: conditions that damage the brain, spinal cord or nerves and disturb control or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 损伤脑、脊髓或神经并扰乱控制或感觉的病症
senses.example: The disease attacks the nervous system and slowly removes movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病攻击神经系统，逐渐夺走运动能力。
senses.why: Clinical language names the whole system when the damage is scattered, because the symptom is a lost function rather than one lesion.
senses.whyCN: 当损伤分散时，临床语言命名整个系统，因为症状是丧失的功能而非单个病灶。

senses.title: Figurative command network
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：组织或经济的指挥网络
senses.definition: the central coordinating network of an organisation, market or machine
senses.definitionCN: 某个组织、市场或机器的中央协调网络
senses.example: Banks form the nervous system of the modern economy.
senses.exampleCN: 银行构成现代经济的神经系统。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows exactly the wiring image: signals run through the whole body and one centre reacts.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用的正是布线意象：信号流遍全身，一个中心作出反应。

intro.en: Nervous system joins nervous, from Latin nervus sinew or nerve, and system, from Greek systema through Late Latin systema. The compound became standard in seventeenth-century anatomy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nervous system 由 nervous（拉丁 nervus「筋、神经」）与 system（经晚期拉丁 systema 上溯希腊 systema）合成。这个复合词在 17 世纪解剖学中成为标准说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew, tendon or cord, and Roman medical writers extended it to the cords they saw carrying sensation and movement.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、腱或索，罗马医学作者把它扩展到他们所见的传导感觉与运动的索状结构。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew or cord and is a cognate of Latin nervus; the two words come from the same earlier root, whose exact form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋或索，与拉丁 nervus 同源；两个词来自同一更早词根，其确切形式属重构。

items.en: The adjective nervosus meant full of sinew, strong or wiry, and English nervous first kept this physical sense before gaining the meaning anxious.
items.cn: 形容词 nervosus 意为多筋的、强健的，英语 nervous 最初保留这一身体义，后来才获得「紧张不安」义。

items.en: Systema meant an organised whole made of parts arranged for one purpose, from syn- together and histanai to set up.
items.cn: systema 意为由为同一目的安排的部分构成的有组织整体，来自 syn-「共同」与 histanai「设立」。

items.en: Seventeenth-century anatomists described the brain, spinal cord and nerves as one system; the exact first English use of the compound is uncertain.
items.cn: 17 世纪解剖学家把脑、脊髓与神经描述为一个系统；这个复合词最早的英语书证年代不确定。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century neurology divided the system into central, peripheral, autonomic and sympathetic parts, and the labels are now standard.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的神经学把该系统分为中枢、外周、自主与交感部分，这些标签如今已标准化。

note.en: The first group holds the words that make up the compound and their close relatives; the second holds other body systems and networks.
note.cn: 第一组是构成复合词的词及其近亲；第二组是其他身体系统与网络。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves, or feeling anxious; it describes and cannot stand for the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的，或感到紧张的；它是描述词，不能代替系统本身。

entries.definition: A single bundle of fibres; the system is the whole network of such bundles plus the brain and cord.
entries.definitionCN: 单束纤维；系统是这类纤维束加上脑与脊髓的整个网络。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or to nerve cells, built on Greek neuron rather than Latin nervus.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的，建立在希腊 neuron 而非拉丁 nervus 之上。

entries.definition: Any organised set of parts; the compound narrows it to the body's signalling network.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有组织的部分集合；复合词把它收窄为身体的信号网络。

entries.definition: The glands that regulate the body through hormones; it works beside the nervous system but uses blood rather than wires.
entries.definitionCN: 通过激素调节身体的腺体系统；它与神经系统并行，但用血液而非线路。

entries.definition: The heart and vessels that move blood; it supplies the nervous system rather than commanding it.
entries.definitionCN: 推动血液的心脏与血管；它为神经系统供血，而非指挥它。

entries.definition: A computing model loosely inspired by neurons; it borrows the name but is not a living nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 受神经元启发而建的计算机模型；它借用名称，但不是活的神经系统。

entries.definition: The central organ of the system; the brain is one component, not the whole network.
entries.definitionCN: 该系统的中心器官；脑是一个组成部分，而非整个网络。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin and Greek cord words, the real anatomy division and the real clinical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁与希腊索状词、真实的解剖划分与真实的临床搭配。

normal.en: Latin nervus and Greek neuron both meant sinew or cord, and both sit behind the modern word nerve.
normal.cn: 拉丁 nervus 与希腊 neuron 都意为筋或索，两者都在现代 nerve 一词背后。

normal.en: The system is divided geographically: central inside the brain and cord, peripheral outside them.
normal.cn: 这个系统按地理位置划分：中枢在脑与脊髓之内，外周在其外。

normal.en: Autonomic means self-governing, and the sympathetic branch is the emergency accelerator.
normal.cn: autonomic 意为自治，sympathetic 支是应急加速器。

normal.en: Nervous system disorder is the clinical umbrella phrase for scattered damage to brain, cord or nerves.
normal.cn: nervous system disorder 是对脑、脊髓或神经分散损伤的临床统称。

normal.en: The metaphor of a command network transfers the wiring image to banks, markets and organisations.
normal.cn: 指挥网络的比喻把布线意象转用到银行、市场与组织上。

abstract.en: Picture a house wired from one fuse box: every room is connected, and one switch can darken all of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋房子从一个配电箱布线：每个房间都连着，一个开关就能让全屋变暗。

abstract.en: Picture two circuits in the same body: one fast and loud for danger, one slow and quiet for rest.
abstract.cn: 想象同一身体里有两套电路：一套遇险时快而响，一套休息时慢而静。

abstract.en: Picture an economy wired like a body, where a signal in one bank moves the whole market.
abstract.cn: 想象一个像身体那样布线的经济体：一家银行的信号能带动整个市场。

examples.en: The nervous system controls movement, sensation and thought.
examples.cn: 神经系统控制运动、感觉与思维。

examples.en: The autonomic nervous system regulates digestion without conscious control.
examples.cn: 自主神经系统在没有意识控制的情况下调节消化。

examples.en: Damage to the nervous system can cause permanent loss of feeling.
examples.cn: 神经系统受损可能造成永久的感觉丧失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nervous（神经的）+ system（系统）」——全身神经接成的一套系统 → 神经系统

root: nervous（拉丁 nervus「筋、神经」）+ system（晚期拉丁 systema，源自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」）；nerve 与希腊 neuron 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the whole wiring, then separate the centre from the periphery, add the automatic and emergency branches, name the signal function, the clinical damage, and finally the metaphor of an organisation's command network.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先讲整套线路，再分出中心与外周，加入自动支与应急支，命名信号功能与临床损伤，最后落到组织指挥网络的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body wired from a central box, every limb connected, every signal answered.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体从一个中央配电箱布线，每条肢体都连着，每个信号都有回应。

branches.en: THE NETWORK AND ITS JOB: the whole wiring, and the messages it carries.
branches.cn: 网络与职责：整套线路，以及它所运送的消息。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY: the deciding centre inside, the connecting nerves outside.
branches.cn: 地理划分：内部的决策中心，外部的连接神经。

branches.en: TWO AUTOMATIC BRANCHES: one keeps the body running, one prepares it for danger.
branches.cn: 两条自动支系：一条维持身体运转，一条为危险作准备。

branches.en: DAMAGE: when the wiring fails, functions disappear before parts do.
branches.cn: 损伤：线路失效时，功能先于部件消失。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR LEAVES THE BODY: banks and markets are wired the same way.
branches.cn: 比喻离开身体：银行与市场也按同样方式布线。

intro.en: The compound joins two borrowed words; the productive part is nervous, whose stem gives nerve, neural and neurology through two different source forms.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个借词连接而成；能产的部分是 nervous，其词干经两种不同来源形式衍生 nerve、neural 与 neurology。

latinIntro.en: Latin nervus sinew gives nerve and nervous; Greek neuron cord gives neural, neuron and neurology; Late Latin systema gives system and systemic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nervus「筋」衍生 nerve 与 nervous；希腊 neuron「索」衍生 neural、neuron 与 neurology；晚期拉丁 systema 衍生 system 与 systemic。

items.example: Latin anatomy used nervus for the cords of the body.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学用 nervus 指身体中的索状结构。

items.meaning: full of sinew; relating to nerves; anxious
items.meaningCN: 多筋的；与神经有关的；紧张不安的
items.example: The nervous system is named with this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 神经系统就用这个形容词命名。

items.structure: Late Latin systema, from Greek systema
items.example: The nerves form one system.
items.exampleCN: 神经构成一个系统。

items.example: Each neuron passes a signal to the next.
items.exampleCN: 每个神经元把信号传给下一个。

items.meaning: relating to nerves or nerve cells
items.meaningCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的
items.example: Neural signals cross the junction in microseconds.
items.exampleCN: 神经信号在极短时间内越过接头。

items.meaning: the study of the nervous system
items.example: Neurology deals with disorders of the nervous system.
items.exampleCN: 神经病学处理神经系统疾病。

items.meaning: around the edge; outside the centre
items.example: The peripheral nervous system lies outside the centre.
items.exampleCN: 外周神经系统位于中心之外。

items.example: The autonomic nervous system governs itself.
items.exampleCN: 自主神经系统自行管理。

items.example: The sympathetic nervous system responds to stress.
items.exampleCN: 交感神经系统对压力作出反应。

latinEntries.structure: Greek neuron, used in Latin medical texts

definition_zh: 神经的；神经系统的；神经元的；神经网络的
definition_en: relating to nerves or to the nervous system, especially to nerve cells and the signals they carry
core_image: 一张由细线与节点连成的网，信号沿线路一跳一跳地传过去
scene: 实验室里，研究员把电极贴上皮肤，屏幕上出现一串随动作起伏的波形： The neural signal rose sharply when the hand moved.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经的、与神经信号有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及神经或神经系统）；句意为手一动，神经信号便急剧上升。

pos.zh: 神经的；与神经或神经系统有关的
神经元的；神经网络式的

senses.title: Relating to nerves
senses.titleCN: 与神经有关的
senses.definition: concerning nerves or the signals that travel along them
senses.definitionCN: 关于神经或沿神经传导的信号的
senses.example: The neural signal rose sharply when the hand moved.
senses.exampleCN: 手一动，神经信号便急剧上升。
senses.why: The adjective points to the wiring itself, so anything it describes belongs to the pathway that carries sensation and command.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指向线路本身，因此它所描述的一切都属于传导感觉与指令的通路。

senses.title: Of the nervous system
senses.titleCN: 神经系统的
senses.definition: belonging to the whole system of brain, spinal cord and nerves
senses.definitionCN: 属于由脑、脊髓与神经构成的整个系统
senses.example: Neural tissue is found from the brain down to the fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 从脑一直到指尖都能找到神经组织。
senses.why: Once the parts are seen as one network, the adjective can describe the network as a whole rather than a single cord.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把这些部分看作一个网络，这个形容词就能描述整个网络，而不只是单根索。

senses.title: Of nerve cells
senses.titleCN: 神经元的；神经细胞的
senses.definition: relating to nerve cells and their connections with one another
senses.definitionCN: 与神经细胞及其相互连接有关的
senses.example: Neural connections form fastest in the first years of life.
senses.exampleCN: 神经连接在生命最初几年形成得最快。
senses.why: At the cellular scale the network is made of individual cells, so the same adjective drops to the level of the node.
senses.whyCN: 在细胞尺度上，网络由一个个细胞组成，因此同一个形容词落到节点的层面。

senses.title: Neural network in computing
senses.titleCN: 神经网络的（计算机领域）
senses.definition: describing a computing model built from layers of simple units loosely modelled on neurons
senses.definitionCN: 描述由多层简单单元构成、粗略模仿神经元的计算模型
senses.example: A neural network learned to recognise faces from thousands of images.
senses.exampleCN: 一个神经网络从数千张图像中学会了识别人脸。
senses.why: The machine borrows the name because its units pass signals to one another in layers, like cells in a living network.
senses.whyCN: 机器借用这个名称，是因为其单元像活体网络中的细胞一样分层传递信号。

senses.title: Neural signal and activity
senses.titleCN: 神经信号与神经活动
senses.definition: the electrical and chemical events by which nerves carry information
senses.definitionCN: 神经携带信息所依靠的电事件与化学事件
senses.example: The recording showed neural activity rising before the word was spoken.
senses.exampleCN: 记录显示，在说岀这个词之前神经活动已经增强。
senses.why: The adjective names the medium rather than the message: what is recorded is the traffic, not its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名媒介而非消息：被记录的是流量，而不是它的意义。

senses.title: Neural development
senses.titleCN: 神经发育的
senses.definition: relating to the growth and wiring of the nervous system before and after birth
senses.definitionCN: 与出生前后神经系统的生长与布线有关的
senses.example: Neural development depends on both genes and early experience.
senses.exampleCN: 神经发育既依赖基因，也依赖早期经历。
senses.why: Development is the process that builds the network, so the adjective marks the period when the wiring is laid down.
senses.whyCN: 发育是搭建网络的过程，因此这个形容词标记线路被铺下的那段时期。

senses.title: Embryological structures
senses.titleCN: 胚胎与解剖结构中的神经（如神经管、神经嵴）
senses.definition: naming embryonic or anatomical structures such as the neural tube and neural crest
senses.definitionCN: 命名神经管、神经嵴等胚胎或解剖结构
senses.example: The neural tube becomes the brain and spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 神经管发育成脑与脊髓。
senses.why: In anatomy the adjective is attached to structures that will become, or belong to, the nervous system.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学中，这个形容词附着于将要成为神经系统或属于神经系统的结构。

senses.title: Neural basis of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 行为或功能的神经基础
senses.definition: the nerve-level mechanism offered as the explanation for a behaviour or ability
senses.definitionCN: 被用来解释某种行为或能力的神经层面机制
senses.example: Researchers look for the neural basis of memory in the hippocampus.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者在海马体中寻找记忆的神经基础。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks an explanatory level: the question is not what happens but which wiring makes it happen.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词标记一个解释层面：问题不是发生了什么，而是哪套线路使之发生。

intro.en: Neural is Greek neuron sinew or nerve plus the Latin-derived adjective ending -al. It became a standard term in nineteenth-century physiology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neural 由希腊 neuron「筋、神经」加拉丁系形容词词尾 -al 构成，在 19 世纪生理学中成为标准术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and Greek medical writers used it for the cords they believed carried feeling and movement.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋、索或神经，希腊医学作者用它指他们认为传导感觉与运动的索状结构。

items.en: Latin nervus meant sinew or cord and is the cognate of Greek neuron; Latin supplied nervous and nerve, while Greek supplied neural and neuron.
items.cn: 拉丁 nervus 意为筋或索，与希腊 neuron 同源；拉丁语提供 nervous 与 nerve，希腊语提供 neural 与 neuron。

items.en: The shared ancestor is reconstructed as a form based on sneu-, meaning sinew; the exact shape is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 共同祖词被重构为以 sneu- 为基础、意为「筋」的形式；确切形态属重构，并非有书证的词。

items.en: The ending -al came to English through Latin -alis and French -al, forming adjectives of relation such as neural and cranial.
items.cn: 词尾 -al 经拉丁 -alis 与法语 -al 进入英语，构成 neural、cranial 这类关系形容词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology needed a word for everything belonging to nerves, and neural filled the gap beside the older nervous.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学需要一个词来指一切属于神经的东西，neural 填补了旧词 nervous 旁边的空位。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of neural is not firmly dated, and the choice between neural and nervous in early texts was not systematic.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：neural 最早的英语书证没有确定年代，早期文献中 neural 与 nervous 的取舍并不系统。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close; the second holds adjectives from neighbouring levels of description.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词；第二组是来自邻近描述层面的形容词。

entries.definition: Taking no side in a dispute, or having no charge; it shares the ending but comes from Latin neuter, neither one nor the other.
entries.definitionCN: 在争端中不站边，或电中性；结尾相同，但来自拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」。

entries.definition: A single nerve cell; neural is the adjective of the whole network or of such cells.
entries.definitionCN: 单个神经细胞；neural 是整个网络或这类细胞的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves, and also meaning anxious; it comes from Latin nervus rather than Greek neuron.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的，也表示紧张不安；它来自拉丁 nervus 而非希腊 neuron。

entries.definition: The medical study of the nervous system; neural describes, neurology names the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究神经系统的医学学科；neural 作描述，neurology 命名学科。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to neurons as cells; neural is broader and can cover the whole network.
entries.definitionCN: 专门与作为细胞的神经元有关；neural 范围更广，可涵盖整个网络。

entries.definition: Relating to the junction where one neuron passes a signal to the next; it is narrower than neural.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经元传递信号的接头有关的；比 neural 更窄。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses and the incoming side of the nerves; neural can describe either direction.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官及神经传入侧有关的；neural 可描述任一方向。

entries.definition: Relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum; neural covers the whole system including the cord and nerves.
entries.definitionCN: 与脑、尤指大脑有关的；neural 涵盖包括脊髓与神经的整个系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real cord roots, the real suffix and the real computing metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的索状词根、真实的后缀与真实的计算比喻。

normal.en: Greek neuron and Latin nervus both meant cord or sinew, so neural and nervous are cousins from two languages.
normal.cn: 希腊 neuron 与拉丁 nervus 都意为索或筋，因此 neural 与 nervous 是来自两种语言的表亲。

normal.en: Neural is the adjective, neuron is the cell, neurology is the discipline.
normal.cn: neural 是形容词，neuron 是细胞，neurology 是学科。

normal.en: Neural network is both a biological web and a computing model that borrows its name.
normal.cn: neural network 既指生物网络，也指借用其名的计算模型。

normal.en: Neural tube and neural crest are fixed embryology terms for structures that become the nervous system.
normal.cn: neural tube 与 neural crest 是固定的胚胎学术语，指发育成神经系统的结构。

normal.en: The phrase neural basis marks the level of explanation, not the thing explained.
normal.cn: neural basis 这一说法标记解释层面，而非被解释的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a net laid over the whole body, every knot connected to every neighbour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满全身的网，每个结都与相邻的结相连。

abstract.en: Picture a signal that is only traffic: it has a route but no meaning until something reads it.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只是流量的信号：它有路线，但在被读取之前没有意义。

abstract.en: Picture a machine built of layers of switches, named after the body it imitates.
abstract.cn: 想象一台由层层开关构成的机器，以它所模仿的身体部位命名。

examples.en: Neural signals travel along the spinal cord within milliseconds.
examples.cn: 神经信号在几毫秒内沿脊髓传导。

examples.en: The team trained a neural network on ten years of weather data.
examples.cn: 团队用十年的天气数据训练了一个神经网络。

examples.en: Neural plasticity allows the brain to adjust after injury.
examples.cn: 神经可塑性使大脑在受伤后得以调整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛柔」（neural）——牛一样韧的细索在全身连成网 → 神经的

root: 希腊 neuron「筋、索、神经」+ 拉丁系形容词词尾 -alis/-al；希腊 neuron 与拉丁 nervus 同源，祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one reference point, the nerve pathway, and shift the scale: the wiring, the whole system, the cell, the computing model, the signal, development, embryology, and the level of explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一个参照点——神经通路，只改变尺度：线路、整个系统、细胞、计算模型、信号、发育、胚胎结构，以及解释层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net of threads and knots, each signal hopping from one knot to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由线与结组成的网，信号从一个结跳到下一个结。

branches.en: THE PATH AND THE WHOLE: one nerve thread, and the system it belongs to.
branches.cn: 通路与整体：一根神经线，以及它所隶属的系统。

branches.en: NODE AND TRAFFIC: the cell that fires, and the signal it sends.
branches.cn: 节点与流量：放电的细胞，以及它发出的信号。

branches.en: THE BORROWED NAME: a computing model made of layered units.
branches.cn: 借来的名称：由分层单元构成的计算模型。

branches.en: BUILDING THE NET: development before birth, and the embryonic structures that start it.
branches.cn: 搭建网络：出生前的发育，以及启动它的胚胎结构。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION LAYER: the wiring offered as the reason for a behaviour.
branches.cn: 解释层：用线路作为某种行为的原因。

intro.en: Neural is a Greek stem with a Latin adjective ending, which is why its relatives split between neuron and nerve.
intro.cn: neural 是希腊词干加拉丁形容词词尾，因此其同族词分成 neuron 与 nerve 两条线。

latinIntro.en: Greek neuron passed into Latin medical writing, and Latin nervus supplies the rival family nerve and nervous; New Latin added neuralis.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 neuron 进入拉丁医学写作，拉丁 nervus 提供另一支 nerve 与 nervous；新拉丁语又添 neuralis。

items.example: The word names both the cord and the cell.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指索，也指细胞。

items.example: The suffix builds adjectives of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Neural tissue runs through the spinal cord.
items.exampleCN: 神经组织贯穿脊髓。

items.example: Anatomical Latin used neuralis for nerve structures.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学拉丁语用 neuralis 指神经结构。

items.example: Each neuron has a body, an axon and dendrites.
items.exampleCN: 每个神经元都有胞体、轴突与树突。

items.example: Neurology became a clinical specialty in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 神经病学在 19 世纪成为临床专科。

items.example: Neuralgia can follow a viral infection.
items.exampleCN: 神经痛可能继发于病毒感染。

items.meaning: the embryonic structure that becomes brain and cord
items.meaningCN: 发育成脑与脊髓的胚胎结构
items.example: The neural tube closes in the first month.
items.exampleCN: 神经管在第一个月内闭合。

items.meaning: a connected set of neurons or of computing units
items.meaningCN: 相互连接的神经元或计算单元集合
items.example: The neural network was trained on labelled images.
items.exampleCN: 这个神经网络用带标签的图像训练。

latinEntries.structure: Greek neuron, used in Latin medical texts

definition_en: a cell of the nervous system that receives signals and passes them on to other nerve cells
core_image: 一个带许多触须的小节点，一头接上线，另一头把信号递出去
scene: 显微镜下，一张神经组织的图里，一个细长的节点伸出许多分支，连向四周： Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经元」这一细胞单位（第 1 个义项：神经系统中传递信号的细胞）；句意为每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。

pos.zh: 神经元；神经细胞（神经系统的基本单元）
（人工神经网络中的）神经元单元

derivatives.zh: 神经毡（神经纤维与胶质构成的网）

senses.title: The nerve cell
senses.titleCN: 神经元：神经系统的基本细胞单位
senses.definition: a cell with a body, one or more long fibres and many branches, which receives and transmits nerve signals
senses.definitionCN: 具有胞体、一条或多条长纤维与许多分支、能接收并传导神经信号的细胞
senses.example: Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。
senses.why: The cell is defined by its shape as much as its tissue: a compact body with a long output line is what makes point-to-point signalling possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个细胞既由组织定义，也由形状定义：紧凑的胞体加一条长输出线，才使点对点传导成为可能。

senses.title: Sensory neuron
senses.titleCN: 感觉神经元：把外界信息送进来
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from a sense organ or receptor toward the central nervous system
senses.definitionCN: 把来自感觉器官或感受器的信号传向中枢神经系统的神经元
senses.example: A sensory neuron reports the heat of the cup to the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经元把杯子的热度报告给脊髓。
senses.why: Direction defines this type: the signal travels inward, so the cell is named for the side it serves.
senses.whyCN: 方向定义了这一类型：信号向内走，因此这个细胞按它所服务的一端命名。

senses.title: Motor neuron
senses.titleCN: 运动神经元：把指令送出去
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from the central nervous system to a muscle or gland
senses.definitionCN: 把信号从中枢神经系统传到肌肉或腺体的神经元
senses.example: A motor neuron tells the hand to close around the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 运动神经元让手合拢握住杯子。
senses.why: This is the mirror image of the sensory type: the same cell structure, with the signal pointed outward.
senses.whyCN: 这是感觉型的镜像：同样的细胞结构，信号朝外指。

senses.title: Interneuron
senses.titleCN: 中间神经元：在系统内部转接
senses.definition: a neuron that connects other neurons inside the central nervous system rather than reaching the body's surface
senses.definitionCN: 在中枢神经系统内部连接其他神经元、不直接到达体表的神经元
senses.example: An interneuron passes the signal from a sensory cell to a motor cell.
senses.exampleCN: 中间神经元把信号从感觉细胞传给运动细胞。
senses.why: Most neurons neither enter nor leave the body; they sit between, which is why the name simply marks the middle position.
senses.whyCN: 大多数神经元既不进入也不离开身体，而是位于中间，因此名称只标记中间位置。

senses.title: Artificial neuron
senses.titleCN: 人工神经元：计算模型中的单元
senses.definition: a simple computing unit that takes several inputs, weights them and passes one output on
senses.definitionCN: 接收若干输入、加权后输出一个信号的简单计算单元
senses.example: Each artificial neuron adds its inputs and fires above a threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人工神经元把输入相加，超过阈值就「放电」。
senses.why: The machine keeps only the input-weight-output shape of the cell, which is why the biological name was borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 机器只保留细胞「输入—加权—输出」的形状，因此借用了生物学名称。

senses.title: Anatomy of a neuron
senses.titleCN: 神经元的解剖形态（胞体、轴突、树突）
senses.definition: the parts of a nerve cell: cell body, axon and dendrites, each with a different role in signalling
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的组成部分：胞体、轴突与树突，各自在传导中承担不同角色
senses.example: The axon of a neuron can be longer than the whole spinal cord segment.
senses.exampleCN: 一个神经元的轴突可能比整段脊髓还长。
senses.why: Once the cell is understood as a device, its parts are named by the direction in which they pass the signal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把细胞理解为装置，它的各部分就按传导方向命名。

senses.title: Neuron degeneration
senses.titleCN: 神经元退化与损伤
senses.definition: the loss or wasting of nerve cells, as in several progressive diseases
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的丧失或萎缩，见于若干进行性疾病
senses.example: The disease slowly destroys the neurons that control walking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病逐渐破坏控制行走的神经元。
senses.why: When cells are lost they are not replaced easily, so clinical talk focuses on the unit rather than the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 细胞丧失后不易补充，因此临床讨论聚焦于这一单位而非整个系统。

senses.title: The functional unit
senses.titleCN: 作为功能单元的神经元
senses.definition: the smallest unit that can receive, integrate and pass on a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 能接收、整合并传出神经信号的最小单位
senses.example: Physiologists treat the neuron as the functional unit of the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 生理学家把神经元视为神经系统的功能单位。
senses.why: A unit is defined by what it can do alone, and a single cell can take in, sum and send a signal.
senses.whyCN: 单位由它能独立完成的事定义，而单个细胞就能接收、汇总并发出信号。

intro.en: Neuron is Greek neuron, meaning sinew, cord or nerve. The modern sense of a nerve cell dates from nineteenth-century microscopy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neuron 即希腊语 neuron，意为筋、索或神经。指神经细胞的现代义来自 19 世纪显微解剖学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and it could name both the string-like structure and the bodily organ of feeling.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋、索或神经，既可指索状结构，也可指身体的感觉器官。

items.en: Latin nervus is the cognate of neuron and supplies the rival English family nerve and nervous; the shared ancestor is reconstructed.
items.cn: 拉丁 nervus 与 neuron 同源，提供英语的另一支 nerve 与 nervous；共同祖形为重构形式。

items.en: Early anatomists used neuron for the nerve fibre or the whole cord, not yet for a single cell.
items.cn: 早期解剖学家用 neuron 指神经纤维或整条索，尚未指单个细胞。

items.en: Improved microscopes and staining showed that nerve tissue is made of discrete cells, and the cell sense of neuron took hold.
items.cn: 显微镜与染色的进步显示神经组织由离散的细胞构成，neuron 的细胞义由此确立。

items.en: The cell sense is usually credited to late nineteenth-century work, including the naming associated with Wilhelm Waldeyer in 1891; the exact first use is debated.
items.cn: 细胞义通常归功于 19 世纪后期的工作，包括 1891 年与 Wilhelm Waldeyer 相关的命名；确切的最早使用仍有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century neuroscience added the artificial neuron and the neuron doctrine, extending the word beyond anatomy.
items.cn: 20 世纪神经科学又添人工神经元与神经元学说，把这个词扩展到解剖学之外。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words and spelling variants; the second holds the parts and neighbours of a neuron.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词与拼写变体；第二组是神经元的部件与邻近结构。

entries.definition: A particle with no charge in an atomic nucleus; it is one letter away in sound but belongs to physics, not biology.
entries.definitionCN: 原子核中不带电的粒子；读音只差一点，却属于物理而非生物。

entries.definition: A British variant spelling of neuron; it is the same cell, not a different structure.
entries.definitionCN: neuron 的英式变体拼写；指同一个细胞，不是另一种结构。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or nerve cells; it describes, while neuron names the cell.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的；它作描述，neuron 命名细胞。

entries.definition: The tangled mass of fibres and glia between nerve cell bodies; it is tissue, not a single cell.
entries.definitionCN: 神经细胞体之间纤维与胶质缠结的团块；它是组织，不是单个细胞。

entries.definition: The everyday term for a neuron; it says what the cell is without using the Greek word.
entries.definitionCN: 神经元的日常说法；不用希腊词而直接说明这个细胞是什么。

entries.definition: The long fibre that carries a signal away from the cell body; it is a part of a neuron.
entries.definitionCN: 把信号从胞体带走的长纤维；它是神经元的一部分。

entries.definition: A branching fibre that receives signals and brings them toward the cell body.
entries.definitionCN: 接收信号并把信号带向胞体的分支纤维。

entries.definition: The gap or junction where one neuron passes a signal to another; it belongs to neither cell alone.
entries.definitionCN: 一个神经元把信号传给另一个的间隙或接头；它不属于任一细胞单独所有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek cord word, the real cell doctrine and the real parts of the cell.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊索状词、真实的细胞学说与真实的细胞部件。

normal.en: Greek neuron meant cord, and a nerve cell is a tiny cord with branches.
normal.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为索，而神经细胞就是一根带分支的微小索。

normal.en: The three functional types are named by direction: sensory in, motor out, interneuron between.
normal.cn: 三种功能类型按方向命名：感觉向内、运动向外、中间神经元居中。

normal.en: Axon carries away, dendrite brings in, and the cell body sits between them.
normal.cn: 轴突带出，树突带入，胞体位于两者之间。

normal.en: An artificial neuron keeps only the shape: inputs, weights, one output.
normal.cn: 人工神经元只保留形状：输入、权重、一个输出。

normal.en: In British spelling the word can also be written neurone, with the same meaning.
normal.cn: 英式拼写也可写作 neurone，意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny switchboard with many incoming wires and one outgoing wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小交换机，许多线进来，一根线出去。

abstract.en: Picture a relay runner who receives a baton and passes it on without keeping it.
abstract.cn: 想象接力跑者，接到棒就传下去，从不把棒留在手里。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd where each person can only whisper to a neighbour, yet a message crosses the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人只能对邻座耳语，消息却能传遍整个房间。

examples.en: A single neuron can connect to thousands of others.
examples.cn: 一个神经元可以连接数千个其他神经元。

examples.en: Motor neurons weaken in the disease that gradually removes movement.
examples.cn: 在那种逐渐夺走运动能力的疾病中，运动神经元会变弱。

examples.en: The model treats each neuron as a simple weighted sum.
examples.cn: 该模型把每个神经元当作一个简单的加权求和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛龙」（neuron）——一头牛身上布满细索，每个结都是一个细胞 → 神经元

root: 希腊 neuron「筋、索、神经」，与拉丁 nervus 同源；指单个神经细胞的现代义形成于 19 世纪显微解剖学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one cell: the basic unit, three directional types, the artificial unit, its anatomy, its degeneration, and finally its status as the functional unit of the system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一个细胞：基本单位、三种方向类型、人工单元、解剖形态、退化损伤，最后是它作为系统功能单位的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small node with many feelers in and one long line out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小节点，许多触须伸进来，一条长线伸出去。

branches.en: THE CELL AND ITS PARTS: the unit as a whole, and the body, axon and dendrites that make it.
branches.cn: 细胞与部件：作为整体的单位，以及构成它的胞体、轴突与树突。

branches.en: THREE DIRECTIONS: inward, outward and between.
branches.cn: 三个方向：向内、向外与居中。

branches.en: THE MACHINE COPY: inputs, weights and one output.
branches.cn: 机器复制品：输入、权重与一个输出。

branches.en: WHEN CELLS DIE: loss of the unit removes the function.
branches.cn: 细胞死亡时：单位的丧失带走功能。

branches.en: WHY IT COUNTS AS A UNIT: it can receive, sum and send on its own.
branches.cn: 为何算作单位：它能独立完成接收、汇总与发出。

intro.en: Neuron is a Greek noun; its English family grows through the suffixes -al, -al + -ly and compounds such as neuropil.
intro.cn: neuron 是希腊名词；其英语词族经 -al、-al + -ly 与 neuropil 这类复合形式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Greek neuron entered Latin medical writing and shares a root with Latin nervus; the adjective neuronalis is a modern scientific formation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 neuron 进入拉丁医学写作，与拉丁 nervus 共享词根；形容词 neuronalis 是现代科学构词。

items.example: The term shifted from the cord to the cell.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「索」转到「细胞」。

items.example: Neuronal loss explains the symptoms.
items.exampleCN: 神经元丧失解释了这些症状。

items.example: The tissue was neuronally organised.
items.exampleCN: 这块组织在神经元层面是有结构的。

items.meaning: the output fibre of a neuron
items.example: The axon carries the signal away.
items.exampleCN: 轴突把信号带走。

items.example: Dendrites spread like small trees.
items.exampleCN: 树突像小树一样展开。

items.example: The synapse passes the signal across a gap.
items.exampleCN: 突触把信号送过间隙。

items.meaning: the felted fibre mass between cell bodies
items.meaningCN: 细胞体之间毡状的纤维团
items.example: Neuropil fills the spaces between neurons.
items.exampleCN: 神经毡填满神经元之间的空隙。

items.example: The marker is neuron-specific.
items.exampleCN: 这个标记是神经元特异性的。

items.meaningCN: 位于其他神经元之间的神经元
items.example: Interneurons relay signals inside the cord.
items.exampleCN: 中间神经元在脊髓内部转接信号。

latinEntries.structure: Greek neuron, used in Latin medical texts

definition_zh: 神经学的；神经系统的；神经科检查的
definition_en: relating to the nervous system or to neurology, the medical study and treatment of it
core_image: 一张把难以看见的神经反应画成曲线的记录纸，让隐藏的故障变得可读
scene: 门诊里，医生用小锤敲膝盖，观察小腿是否自动弹起： The doctor ordered a neurological examination after the fall.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经系统的、神经科的」（第 1 个义项：与神经系统及其医学检查有关）；句意为跌倒之后，医生安排了一次神经科检查。

pos.zh: 神经系统的；与神经病学有关的
神经科检查或治疗的

derivatives.zh: 在神经学意义上；神经方面地

senses.title: Relating to the nervous system
senses.titleCN: 神经系统的（医学语境）
senses.definition: concerning the nervous system, its functions or its diseases
senses.definitionCN: 关于神经系统、其功能或疾病的
senses.example: The doctor ordered a neurological examination after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 跌倒之后，医生安排了一次神经科检查。
senses.why: The adjective marks the domain rather than the organ: it says which system the question belongs to before saying what is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记领域而非器官：它先说问题属于哪个系统，再说哪里出了问题。

senses.title: Of the discipline of neurology
senses.titleCN: 神经病学的（学科语境）
senses.definition: belonging to neurology as a branch of medicine and research
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为医学与研究分支的神经病学
senses.example: The paper appears in a neurological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一本神经学杂志上。
senses.why: Once a discipline has a name, its adjective also labels journals, societies and methods, not only patients.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科有了名称之后，其形容词也标记期刊、学会与方法，而不只是病人。

senses.title: Neurological examination
senses.titleCN: 神经科检查
senses.definition: the physical tests of reflexes, sensation, coordination and strength used to assess nerves
senses.definitionCN: 通过反射、感觉、协调与力量等体检来评估神经的方式
senses.example: A neurological examination tested her reflexes and balance.
senses.exampleCN: 一次神经科检查测试了她的反射与平衡。
senses.why: The nervous system is hard to see directly, so clinicians infer its state from a standard set of observable responses.
senses.whyCN: 神经系统难以直接看见，因此临床医生靠一组可观察的标准反应来推断其状态。

senses.title: Neurological disorder
senses.titleCN: 神经系统疾病
senses.definition: a disease of the brain, spinal cord or nerves that disturbs movement, feeling or thought
senses.definitionCN: 影响脑、脊髓或神经，扰乱运动、感觉或思维的疾病
senses.example: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder with many causes.
senses.exampleCN: 癫痫是一种病因多样的神经系统疾病。
senses.why: The word groups many different lesions under the system they share, which is why it is an umbrella term.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按照共同所属的系统把许多不同病灶归为一类，因此是统称。

senses.title: Neurological damage
senses.titleCN: 神经损伤（后遗影响）
senses.definition: harm to nerve tissue that leaves a lasting deficit in movement, sensation or cognition
senses.definitionCN: 对神经组织的损害，留下运动、感觉或认知上的持久缺陷
senses.example: The infection left neurological damage that affected her speech.
senses.exampleCN: 感染留下了神经损伤，影响了她的言语。
senses.why: Damage is described by the system it strikes because the deficit may appear far from the original injury.
senses.whyCN: 损伤按所打击的系统来描述，因为缺陷出现的位置可能远离最初的伤处。

senses.title: Neurological development
senses.titleCN: 神经发育（儿童发育语境）
senses.definition: the growth and maturing of the nervous system, especially in early childhood
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统的生长与成熟，尤指幼儿期
senses.example: Early nutrition affects neurological development in children.
senses.exampleCN: 早期营养影响儿童的神经发育。
senses.why: Development is tracked through the functions the system should acquire, so the adjective names the expected trajectory.
senses.whyCN: 发育按该系统应当获得的功用来追踪，因此这个形容词命名预期的轨迹。

senses.title: Neurological basis
senses.titleCN: 神经机制层面的（解释语境）
senses.definition: the nerve-level mechanism proposed as the explanation of a symptom or ability
senses.definitionCN: 被提出来解释某种症状或能力的神经层面机制
senses.example: The tremor has a neurological basis rather than a psychological one.
senses.exampleCN: 这种震颤有神经机制上的基础，而非心理原因。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks a level of explanation and contrasts with other possible levels such as the social or the psychological.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词标记解释层面，并与心理、社会等其他层面形成对照。

senses.title: Neurological treatment
senses.titleCN: 神经科治疗（临床处置语境）
senses.definition: medical care directed at the nervous system, such as drugs, surgery or rehabilitation
senses.definitionCN: 针对神经系统的医疗处置，如药物、手术或康复
senses.example: Neurological treatment began with drugs to control the seizures.
senses.exampleCN: 神经科治疗先用药物控制癫痫发作。
senses.why: Treatment is classified by the system it targets, so the adjective also appears in care plans and referrals.
senses.whyCN: 治疗按所针对的系统分类，因此这个形容词也出现在照护计划与转诊中。

intro.en: Neurological is neurology plus -ical. Neurology joins Greek neuron nerve and -logia study. The English word became clinical in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neurological 由 neurology 加 -ical 构成。neurology 由希腊 neuron「神经」与 -logia「研究」合成。这个英语词在 19 世纪转为临床用语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve and was the word Greek doctors used for the body's signal cords.
items.cn: neuron 意为筋、索或神经，是希腊医生指身体信号索的用词。

items.en: The ending -logia meant the study or account of something, built on logos word, reason or account.
items.cn: 词尾 -logia 意为对某物的研究或论述，建立在 logos「言词、理性、论述」之上。

items.en: New Latin formed neurologia for the study of nerves; early uses were often theoretical rather than clinical.
items.cn: 新拉丁语构成 neurologia，指对神经的研究；早期用法多偏理论而非临床。

items.en: English neurology appears in seventeenth-century medical writing, but its modern clinical sense is later.
items.cn: 英语 neurology 出现在 17 世纪医学写作中，但其现代临床义更晚。

items.en: The ending -ical, from Latin -icalis, built the adjective neurological, meaning belonging to that study.
items.cn: 词尾 -ical 来自拉丁 -icalis，构成形容词 neurological，意为属于这门研究。

items.en: Neurology became a recognised hospital specialty in the nineteenth century, and neurological spread to examinations, disorders and wards. The exact first clinical uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 神经病学在 19 世纪成为受承认的医院专科，neurological 随之扩展到检查、疾病与病房。确切的最早临床用法存疑。

note.en: The first group holds same-stem forms and near spellings; the second holds adjectives for adjacent medical or mental domains.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干形式与形近拼写；第二组是邻近医学或精神领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; neurological is its adjective, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；neurological 是其形容词，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: A doctor who practises neurology; the adjective describes the field, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 从事神经病学的医生；形容词描述领域，而非人。

entries.definition: Relating to nephrology, the study of the kidneys; the prefix nephro- replaces neuro- and changes the organ entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 与肾脏学有关的；前缀 nephro- 取代 neuro-，器官完全不同。

entries.definition: Historically a term for nervous or anxiety-related mental disturbance; it is psychological in use, not a medical description of nerve tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上指与紧张或焦虑相关的精神障碍；使用上属心理层面，并非对神经组织的医学描述。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves, though it also means anxious; neurological is the clinical and systematic counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的，但也表示紧张；neurological 是更临床、更系统的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or nerve cells; neural often describes mechanisms, while neurological describes medicine and disorders.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的；neural 常描述机制，neurological 描述医学与疾病。

entries.definition: Relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum; neurological covers brain, cord and nerves together.
entries.definitionCN: 与脑、尤指大脑有关的；neurological 涵盖脑、脊髓与神经。

entries.definition: Relating to mental illness and its treatment; it is a neighbouring field, not a synonym, because the focus is behaviour rather than nerve tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病及其治疗有关的；它是邻近领域而非同义词，因为焦点在行为而非神经组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek stems, the real clinical phrases and the real hospital split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词干、真实的临床搭配与真实的医院分科。

normal.en: neuron + -logia + -ical: the study of nerves turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: neuron + -logia + -ical：把「对神经的研究」变成形容词。

normal.en: Neurology is the field, a neurologist is the doctor, and neurological is the adjective.
normal.cn: neurology 是领域，neurologist 是医生，neurological 是形容词。

normal.en: The fixed phrases are a ladder: examination, disorder, damage, symptoms, development, assessment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配构成一条阶梯：检查、疾病、损伤、症状、发育、评估。

normal.en: Nephrological looks almost the same but belongs to the kidneys, so the first three letters decide the organ.
normal.cn: nephrological 看起来几乎一样，却属于肾脏，因此前三个字母决定器官。

normal.en: Psychiatric and neurological are neighbouring wards, not the same ward.
normal.cn: 精神科与神经科是相邻病房，而不是同一间病房。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of tiny waves drawn from a body that cannot show its wiring directly.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由无法直接显露线路的身体画出的细微波形图。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor tapping a knee to ask the nerves a question they must answer by reflex.
abstract.cn: 想象医生敲一下膝盖，向神经提出一个只能靠反射回答的问题。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, one marked nerves and one marked mind; the adjectives decide which door.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两扇门，一扇标神经，一扇标心智；形容词决定走哪扇。

examples.en: The patient was referred for a neurological assessment.
examples.cn: 这位病人被转去做神经功能评估。

examples.en: Neurological disorders range from migraine to epilepsy.
examples.cn: 神经系统疾病的范围从偏头痛到癫痫。

examples.en: The team studies neurological development in premature infants.
examples.cn: 该团队研究早产儿的神经发育。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛柔_logic」（neurological）——研究牛一样韧的神经索的学问 → 神经学的

root: neurology（希腊 neuron「神经」+ -logia「研究」）+ -ical；英语 neurology 见于 17 世纪，现代临床义定型于 19 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses work as labels: the system, the discipline, the examination, the disorder, the damage, the development, the explanatory level and the treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是标签：系统、学科、检查、疾病、损伤、发育、解释层面与治疗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper trace that makes hidden nerve activity readable.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张把隐藏的神经活动变得可读的记录纸。

branches.en: TWO CONTEXTS: the system in a patient, and the discipline in a journal.
branches.cn: 两种语境：病人身上的系统，以及期刊里的学科。

branches.en: BEFORE AND DURING LIFE: an examination that asks, and a development that is watched.
branches.cn: 生前与生中：提出问题的检查，以及被观察的发育。

branches.en: FAILURE: a named disorder, and the lasting damage it leaves.
branches.cn: 失效：具名的疾病，以及它留下的持久损伤。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION LAYER: a neurological basis is contrasted with a psychological one.
branches.cn: 解释层：神经基础与心理基础形成对照。

branches.en: RESPONSE: treatment is classified by the system it aims at.
branches.cn: 回应：治疗按所针对的系统分类。

intro.en: Neurological stacks three pieces: neuron nerve, -logia study, and -ical relating to. Each can be read separately.
intro.cn: neurological 叠了三段：neuron「神经」、-logia「研究」与 -ical「与……有关的」，每一段都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: New Latin neurologia combined Greek neuron with -logia, and Latin -icalis supplied the adjective ending; the same pieces build neurological in English.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁 neurologia 把希腊 neuron 与 -logia 结合，拉丁 -icalis 提供形容词词尾；同样的部件在英语中构成 neurological。

items.example: The stem names the body's signal cords.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名身体的信号索。

items.example: The suffix names a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门学科。

items.example: The suffix turns the discipline into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科变成形容词。

items.meaning: the study of the nervous system
items.example: Neurology has its own wards and journals.
items.exampleCN: 神经病学有自己的病房与期刊。

items.example: The neurological examination tested her reflexes.
items.exampleCN: 神经科检查测试了她的反射。

items.example: The neurologist reviewed the scan.
items.exampleCN: 神经科医生查看了影像。

items.example: The patient is neurologically stable.
items.exampleCN: 这位病人神经方面情况稳定。

items.example: Neuropathy causes numbness in the feet.
items.exampleCN: 神经病引起足部麻木。

items.meaning: the scientific study of the nervous system
items.example: Neuroscience combines biology, psychology and medicine.
items.exampleCN: 神经科学结合生物学、心理学与医学。
