definition_zh: 脑；大脑；智力；聪明人；（组织的）核心
definition_en: the organ inside the head that controls thought, memory, feeling and movement, or the intelligence associated with it
core_image: 一团折叠的线路，所有信号在这里汇合、比较，再下达指令
scene: 孩子指着自己的头，问为什么睡着以后还会做梦： The brain keeps working even while the body sleeps.
sceneCN: 这里指「脑」这一器官（第 1 个义项：控制思维、记忆与运动的器官）；句意为即使身体睡去，脑仍在工作。

pos.zh: 脑；大脑（器官）
智力；头脑；聪明人；（组织的）核心人物

senses.title: The organ in the head
senses.titleCN: 脑：颅内的控制器官
senses.definition: the organ inside the skull that controls thought, memory, emotion and movement
senses.definitionCN: 位于颅骨内、控制思维、记忆、情绪与运动的器官
senses.example: The brain keeps working even while the body sleeps.
senses.exampleCN: 即使身体睡去，脑仍在工作。
senses.why: The primary sense names the physical organ, and every other sense borrows something from it: its power, its products or its position.
senses.whyCN: 首要义项命名实体器官，其余义项都从它借走某样东西：力量、产物或位置。

senses.title: Intelligence
senses.titleCN: 智力；头脑
senses.definition: the ability to think, learn and solve problems
senses.definitionCN: 思考、学习与解决问题的能力
senses.example: She has the brain for advanced mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 她有学高等数学的头脑。
senses.why: Because thinking happens in the organ, the organ's name stands for the ability, just as muscle can stand for strength.
senses.whyCN: 因为思考发生在该器官中，器官名就代表这种能力，正如「肌肉」一词可代表力量。

senses.title: A clever person
senses.titleCN: 聪明人；智囊
senses.definition: a very intelligent person, especially one who supplies ideas to a group
senses.definitionCN: 非常聪明的人，尤指为团体出主意的人
senses.example: The company hired the best brains in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了该领域最聪明的人。
senses.why: The part stands for the person: a group of brains means a group of thinkers, not a collection of organs.
senses.whyCN: 部分代指整体：这个说法指一群思考者，而非一堆器官。

senses.title: The core of an operation
senses.titleCN: 组织的核心；幕后主脑
senses.definition: the person or small group that plans and directs an operation
senses.definitionCN: 策划并指挥某项行动的人或小团体
senses.example: She was the brains behind the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 她是整个运动的幕后主脑。
senses.why: The organ that issues commands becomes a metaphor for the command centre of any organised effort.
senses.whyCN: 下达指令的器官成为任何有组织行动之指挥中心的比喻。

senses.title: The control unit of a machine
senses.titleCN: 机器的中央控制部分
senses.definition: the part of a machine or system that processes information and gives orders
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统中处理信息并发出指令的部分
senses.example: The chip is the brain of the new robot.
senses.exampleCN: 这块芯片是新机器人的大脑。
senses.why: A machine with a central processor copies the body's arrangement, so the organ name moves to the processor.
senses.whyCN: 带中央处理器的机器复制了身体的布局，因此器官名转到处理器上。

senses.title: Animal brain as food
senses.titleCN: 食用动物脑
senses.definition: the brain of an animal cooked and eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物烹调的动物脑
senses.example: The market sold lamb brains beside the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 市场上在鱼旁边卖羊脑。
senses.why: Food language keeps the plain physical sense, usually in the plural, with no metaphor attached.
senses.whyCN: 食物语言保留朴素的实体义，常用复数，不带比喻。

senses.title: Mental work
senses.titleCN: 脑力劳动；苦思
senses.definition: thinking effort, especially when it is hard or prolonged
senses.definitionCN: 思考上的努力，尤指艰难或持久的思考
senses.example: We racked our brains for a solution all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整晚绞尽脑汁想办法。
senses.why: The organ is treated as a tool that can be worn out by use, which is why the phrase suggests strain.
senses.whyCN: 器官被当作会因使用而疲惫的工具，因此这个说法暗示费力。

senses.title: Talent in brain drain
senses.titleCN: 人才（人才外流语境）
senses.definition: skilled and educated people, thought of as a national resource that can leave
senses.definitionCN: 被视为可能流失的国家资源的技术与受教育人才
senses.example: The country lost many of its best brains to foreign labs.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家许多最优秀的人才流失到了国外实验室。
senses.why: In brain drain the word counts people as movable intellectual capital, so the organ name becomes an economic category.
senses.whyCN: 在「人才外流」这一说法中，这个词把人才当作可流动的智力资本，器官名由此变成经济范畴。

intro.en: Brain is native Old English braegen, from Proto-Germanic and ultimately from an Indo-European root for brain or skull. It has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin cerebrum is a different root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: brain 是古英语本族词 brægen，来自原始日耳曼语，更早可追溯到表示脑或颅的印欧词根。它没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁 cerebrum 属另一词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English braegen or brægen meant the brain, and related forms named the crown of the skull.
items.cn: 古英语 braegen 或 brægen 意为脑，相关形式也指颅顶。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as bragnam or bragnan, the source of the Germanic words for brain; the form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 其祖形被重构为 bragnam 或 bragnan，是日耳曼诸语「脑」一词的来源；这一形式属重构。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as mregh-m(n)o-, meaning brain or skull; only the reconstruction exists, not an attested word.
items.cn: 更深词根被重构为 mregh-m(n)o-，意为脑或颅；只存在重构形式，没有书证词。

items.en: Greek bregma meant the front part of the skull, and it is sometimes linked to the same root; the link is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 希腊 bregma 意为颅骨前部，有时被认为同出这一词根；这一联系是假说，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin cerebrum brain is a separate word with its own uncertain origin, so it is not a Latin cognate of brain; cerebral belongs to that other line.
items.cn: 拉丁 cerebrum「脑」是另一个词，来源亦不确定，因此不是 brain 的拉丁同族词；cerebral 属于另一条线。

items.en: The senses of intelligence, mastermind and machine processor developed in later English, with the exact dates of each figurative branch uncertain.
items.cn: 智力、幕后主脑与机器处理器等义项在后世英语中发展出来，各比喻支线的确切年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words and close compounds; the second holds words for mind and intellect that are often swapped for brain.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词与近亲复合词；第二组是常与 brain 互换的心智与智力词。

entries.definition: A term in string theory for a extended object; it sounds exactly like brain but belongs to physics.
entries.definitionCN: 弦理论中表示延展对象的术语；读音与 brain 完全相同，却属于物理。

entries.definition: Muscular strength or heavy muscle; it is the body's force as opposed to the brain's intelligence.
entries.definitionCN: 肌肉力量或厚实肌肉；它代表身体的力量，与脑的智力相对。

entries.definition: Clever, full of brains; it describes a person, while brain names the organ or the ability.
entries.definitionCN: 聪明的、有头脑的；它描述人，而 brain 命名器官或能力。

entries.definition: An idea or project produced by one person's mind; the compound keeps the metaphor of mental production.
entries.definitionCN: 由某人的头脑产生的想法或项目；这个复合词保留「心智产物」的比喻。

entries.definition: The seat of thought and awareness; it overlaps brain in everyday use but does not name the physical organ.
entries.definitionCN: 思维与意识的所在；日常用法与 brain 重叠，但不命名实体器官。

entries.definition: The main upper part of the brain in anatomy; it is one region of the brain, from a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 解剖学上脑的主要上部；它是脑的一个区域，来自不同的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The power of reasoning, considered abstractly; brain can mean this too, but intellect never means the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象的推理能力；brain 也可指这种能力，但 intellect 从不指器官。

entries.definition: The whole upper part of the body; the brain sits inside the head, so the two are not synonyms.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的上部整体；脑位于头内，两者并非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English word, the real Germanic reconstruction, and the real modern compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语词、真实的日耳曼重构形式与真实的现代复合词。

normal.en: Old English braegen is the direct source, and the modern spelling keeps the same one-syllable shape.
normal.cn: 古英语 braegen 是直接来源，现代拼写保留同样的单音节形状。

normal.en: Latin cerebrum is not the source of brain; it gives cerebral and cerebrum, a separate line.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cerebrum 不是 brain 的来源；它衍生 cerebral 与 cerebrum，属另一条线。

normal.en: Brainy and brainless split the quality: one means clever, the other means stupid.
normal.cn: brainy 与 brainless 把这种性质分成两端：一个聪明，一个愚蠢。

normal.en: Brain drain, brain wave and brainstorm all treat the organ as a source of people or ideas.
normal.cn: brain drain、brain wave、brainstorm 都把该器官当作人才或想法的来源。

normal.en: Rack one's brains keeps the physical image of an organ strained by use.
normal.cn: rack one's brains 保留了器官因使用而紧绷的身体意象。

abstract.en: Picture a folded map of wires where every road meets every other road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折叠的线路地图，每条路都与其他路相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a command room inside a body, receiving reports and sending orders.
abstract.cn: 想象身体内部的一间指挥室，接收报告并发出命令。

abstract.en: Picture a country losing its engineers the way a body might lose its nerve.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家失去工程师，正如身体失去神经。

examples.en: The brain processes signals from the senses within milliseconds.
examples.cn: 脑在几毫秒内处理来自感官的信号。

examples.en: She was the brains behind the new design.
examples.cn: 她是这项新设计背后的主脑。

examples.en: The country is trying to stop the brain drain of young scientists.
examples.cn: 这个国家正试图阻止年轻科学家的外流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不来」（brain）——不来大脑就转不动 → 脑；智力

root: 古英语 brægen「脑」，来自原始日耳曼语 bragnam（重构形式），更早印欧词根 mregh-m(n)o-（重构形式）；无可靠拉丁同族词，拉丁 cerebrum 属另一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one organ: the organ itself, intelligence, a clever person, the mastermind of a plan, a machine's control unit, food, hard thinking, and talent counted as national capital.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官向外辐射：器官本身、智力、聪明人、计划的主脑、机器的控制部件、食物、苦思，以及被当作国家资本的人才。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded network inside the skull where signals meet, compare and issue orders.
core.cn: 核心意象：颅骨内一张折叠的网络，信号在此汇合、比较并下达指令。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL ORGAN: the working brain, and the same tissue as food.
branches.cn: 实体器官：工作的脑，以及作为食物的同一组织。

branches.en: ABILITY AND EFFORT: intelligence as a capacity, and hard thinking as strain.
branches.cn: 能力与费力：作为能力的智力，以及作为消耗的苦思。

branches.en: PART FOR PERSON: clever individuals, and the one who plans for a group.
branches.cn: 部分代指人：聪明个体，以及为团体谋划的那一位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE ANALOGY: a processor becomes the brain of a device.
branches.cn: 机器类比：处理器成为设备的大脑。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS CAPITAL: talent can be counted, attracted and lost.
branches.cn: 人才即资本：人才可以被计数、吸引与流失。

intro.en: Brain is a native Germanic noun with no reliable Latin cognate, so it builds compounds rather than prefix families.
intro.cn: brain 是日耳曼语本族名词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此它构成复合词而非前缀词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established. Latin cerebrum brain comes from a different root and gives cerebral, cerebrum and cerebellum; it must not be presented as the source of brain.
latinIntro.cn: 没有已确立的拉丁同族词。拉丁 cerebrum「脑」来自另一词根，衍生 cerebral、cerebrum 与 cerebellum；不得把它说成 brain 的来源。

items.example: The brain keeps working during sleep.
items.exampleCN: 脑在睡眠中仍在工作。

items.example: The brainy student solved it first.
items.exampleCN: 那个聪明的学生最先解出。

items.example: It was a brainless decision.
items.exampleCN: 那是个不动脑的决定。

items.example: The festival was her brainchild.
items.exampleCN: 这个节庆是她的创意产物。

items.meaning: a burst of ideas from a group
items.example: The team held a brainstorm on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 团队周一开了头脑风暴会。

items.meaning: the loss of skilled people from a country
items.example: The brain drain slowed after salaries rose.
items.exampleCN: 薪资提高后人才外流放缓。

items.meaning: an electrical rhythm of the brain; also a sudden idea
items.meaningCN: 脑电节律；也指突然的灵感
items.example: The brain wave was recorded during sleep.
items.exampleCN: 睡眠期间记录到了脑波。

items.meaning: the stalk of tissue joining brain and spinal cord
items.meaningCN: 连接脑与脊髓的柄状组织
items.example: The brainstem controls basic breathing.
items.exampleCN: 脑干控制基本呼吸。

items.meaning: an image of the brain made by a machine
items.meaningCN: 用机器生成的脑部影像
items.example: The brain scan showed no bleeding.
items.exampleCN: 脑部扫描未显示出血。

definition_zh: 大脑的；脑的；理智的；需要脑力的
definition_en: relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum, or to thinking rather than feeling
core_image: 颅骨里那团折叠的组织在冷光下显出沟回，像一张思考的地图
scene: 医生指着影像上颅骨内的一层灰白色结构，解释出血的位置： The scan showed a small bleed in the cerebral cortex.
sceneCN: 这里指「大脑的、与大脑皮层有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及脑或大脑）；句意为扫描显示大脑皮层有一处小出血。

pos.zh: 大脑的；脑的（解剖义）
理智的；偏重思考而非情感的

senses.title: Relating to the brain
senses.titleCN: 大脑的；脑的（解剖义）
senses.definition: concerning the brain, especially the main upper part of it
senses.definitionCN: 关于脑、尤指脑的主要上部
senses.example: The scan showed a small bleed in the cerebral cortex.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示大脑皮层有一处小出血。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the organ itself, so in medicine it marks anything located in or belonging to the brain.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于器官本身，因此在医学中标记位于脑内或属于脑的一切。

senses.title: Cerebral cortex
senses.titleCN: 大脑皮层的
senses.definition: relating to the outer layer of the brain where much processing and conscious thought occurs
senses.definitionCN: 与脑的外层有关，大量加工与有意识思维在此发生
senses.example: Cerebral cortex activity increased during the memory task.
senses.exampleCN: 在记忆任务中，大脑皮层活动增强。
senses.why: The cortex is the brain's surface, so the adjective plus cortex names the exact sheet where thought is computed.
senses.whyCN: 皮层是脑的表面，因此这个形容词加「皮层」精确命名思维被计算的那一层。

senses.title: Cerebral blood vessels
senses.titleCN: 脑血管与脑部病变的
senses.definition: relating to the blood vessels and circulation inside the brain
senses.definitionCN: 与脑内血管及其循环有关的
senses.example: A cerebral haemorrhage is bleeding inside the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 脑出血是脑内出血。
senses.why: Clinical compounds use the adjective to say where the vessel or bleed lies, which determines the danger.
senses.whyCN: 临床复合词用这个形容词说明血管或出血的位置，而位置决定危险程度。

senses.title: Intellectual rather than emotional
senses.titleCN: 理智的；偏重思考的
senses.definition: appealing to thought rather than to feeling, said of art, music or a person's style
senses.definitionCN: 诉诸思考而非情感，用于艺术、音乐或某人的风格
senses.example: The film is cerebral and slow, with little action.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影偏重思辨、节奏缓慢，几乎没有动作。
senses.why: Since the brain is the organ of reasoning, calling a work cerebral says it addresses the head rather than the heart.
senses.whyCN: 既然脑是推理的器官，把作品称为「理智型」就是说它诉诸头脑而非心灵。

senses.title: Demanding mental work
senses.titleCN: 需要脑力的
senses.definition: requiring sustained thought and concentration rather than physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 需要持续思考与专注，而非体力
senses.example: Proofreading is cerebral work that leaves you tired but not sweaty.
senses.exampleCN: 校对是需要脑力的工作，让人累却不流汗。
senses.why: Work is classified by the organ it uses, so a task that consumes attention is called cerebral.
senses.whyCN: 工作按所使用的器官分类，因此消耗注意力的任务被称为「脑力型」。

senses.title: Cerebral palsy
senses.titleCN: 脑瘫（固定医学术语）
senses.definition: a group of movement disorders caused by damage to the brain before, during or shortly after birth
senses.definitionCN: 由出生前、出生时或出生后不久脑损伤引起的一组运动障碍
senses.example: Cerebral palsy affects movement but not necessarily intelligence.
senses.exampleCN: 脑瘫影响运动，但不一定影响智力。
senses.why: The fixed term names the organ where the damage occurred, not the limbs where the difficulty shows.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定术语命名损伤发生的器官，而不是困难显现的肢体。

senses.title: Cerebral hemispheres
senses.titleCN: 大脑半球的（解剖分区）
senses.definition: relating to the two halves of the brain and their different roles
senses.definitionCN: 与脑的两半及其不同角色有关的
senses.example: The cerebral hemispheres are linked by a band of fibres.
senses.exampleCN: 两个大脑半球由一条纤维带相连。
senses.why: Anatomy divides the organ into halves, and the adjective marks the level at which the division is made.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把该器官分成两半，这个形容词标记作此划分的层面。

senses.title: Cerebral evolution
senses.titleCN: 大脑演化的（比较解剖语境）
senses.definition: relating to the size and structure of the brain across species and over time
senses.definitionCN: 与不同物种及不同时期脑的大小和结构有关的
senses.example: Cerebral size increased in several primate lineages.
senses.exampleCN: 在若干灵长类谱系中，脑的尺寸增大。
senses.why: Comparative biology uses the adjective to compare organs across species, so it marks a scale larger than one patient.
senses.whyCN: 比较生物学用这个形容词跨物种比较器官，因此它标记比单个病人更大的尺度。

intro.en: Cerebral comes from Latin cerebrum brain plus -al. The origin of cerebrum itself is uncertain, and it is not the source of the Germanic word brain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cerebral 来自拉丁 cerebrum「脑」加 -al。cerebrum 本身的来源不确定，它也不是日耳曼语 brain 的来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cerebrum was the ordinary Latin word for the brain, and the diminutive cerebellum named the little brain at the back of the skull.
items.cn: cerebrum 是拉丁语中表示脑的普通名词，指小形式 cerebellum 则命名颅后的小脑。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of cerebrum is not established. A link to Greek kara head has been suggested, but it is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：cerebrum 的更深来源未获确立。有人提出它与希腊 kara「头」有关，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Scientific Latin formed cerebralis belonging to the brain, the direct model for English cerebral.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语构成 cerebralis，意为属于脑的，是英语 cerebral 的直接模型。

items.en: English anatomy adopted cerebral in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries for structures inside the skull.
items.cn: 英语解剖学在 17 与 18 世纪采用 cerebral 指颅内的结构。

items.en: The sense of intellectual rather than emotional developed in the nineteenth century, when critics began to describe art as addressing the head.
items.cn: 指理智而非情感的义项在 19 世纪发展起来，当时评论家开始说艺术诉诸头脑。

items.en: Modern medicine fixed phrases such as cerebral cortex, cerebral palsy and cerebral haemorrhage; the exact first uses of each are uncertain.
items.cn: 现代医学固定了 cerebral cortex、cerebral palsy、cerebral haemorrhage 等说法；各说法确切的最早使用存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the Latin brain stem or close in sound; the second holds adjectives for thinking and for neighbouring body regions.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在拉丁「脑」词干上或读音接近的词；第二组是表示思考及邻近身体部位的形容词。

entries.definition: A grain food such as wheat or oats; it sounds close but comes from Ceres, the goddess of grain, not from cerebrum.
entries.definitionCN: 小麦、燕麦等谷物食品；读音接近，但来自谷神刻瑞斯，而非 cerebrum。

entries.definition: The anatomical name for the main part of the brain; cerebral is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 脑主要部分的解剖名称；cerebral 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: The little brain at the back of the skull, a diminutive of cerebrum; it is a different structure.
entries.definitionCN: 颅后的小脑，是 cerebrum 的指小形式；它是另一种结构。

entries.definition: Relating to brain and spine together; it joins cerebral with spinal and covers a wider region.
entries.definitionCN: 同时涉及脑与脊髓的；它把 cerebral 与 spinal 连接，覆盖范围更广。

entries.definition: Relating to reasoning and ideas; it is close to the figurative cerebral but never describes the organ itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与推理和观念有关的；接近 cerebral 的比喻义，但从不描述器官本身。

entries.definition: Relating to mental processes such as memory and perception; it names the processes rather than the tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 与记忆、知觉等心理过程有关的；它命名过程而非组织。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves anywhere in the body; cerebral is limited to the brain.
entries.definitionCN: 与全身神经有关的；cerebral 仅限于脑。

entries.definition: Based on reason; it describes the quality of thinking, while cerebral can also describe the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 基于理性的；它描述思维的性质，而 cerebral 也可描述器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin brain noun, the real diminutive and the real clinical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「脑」名词、真实的指小形式与真实的临床搭配。

normal.en: Cerebrum is Latin for brain, and cerebral is its adjective; the pair works like cerebrum and cerebral in anatomy.
normal.cn: cerebrum 是拉丁语「脑」，cerebral 是其形容词；这对词在解剖学中成对使用。

normal.en: Cerebellum is the diminutive of cerebrum, so the little brain sits at the back of the skull.
normal.cn: cerebellum 是 cerebrum 的指小形式，因此「小脑」位于颅后。

normal.en: Cerebral cortex, cerebral palsy and cerebral haemorrhage are fixed medical phrases, each naming a place in the head.
normal.cn: cerebral cortex、cerebral palsy、cerebral haemorrhage 都是固定医学说法，各自命名头内的一个位置。

normal.en: Cereal is not related: it comes from the goddess of grain, so the first vowel and the meaning both differ.
normal.cn: cereal 与此无关：它来自谷神，因此首个元音与意义都不同。

normal.en: Latin cerebrum is not the source of English brain; the two are separate words for the same organ.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cerebrum 不是英语 brain 的来源；两者是同一器官的两个独立词。

abstract.en: Picture a folded grey map lit from inside, with every crease a route.
abstract.cn: 想象一张从内部照亮的灰色折叠地图，每道褶都是一条路线。

abstract.en: Picture a film with no chase scenes, only two people thinking in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象一部没有追逐场面的电影，只有两个人在安静的房间里思考。

abstract.en: Picture a hemisphere split down the middle, each half talking to the other through a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从中间分开的半球，两半通过一座桥交谈。

examples.en: Cerebral blood flow falls during a stroke.
examples.cn: 中风时脑血流量下降。

examples.en: The novel is cerebral, full of argument and little action.
examples.cn: 这部小说偏重思辨，充满论辩而少有行动。

examples.en: Cerebral palsy results from damage to the brain early in life.
examples.cn: 脑瘫源于生命早期脑部受损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞瑞不柔」（cerebral）——塞满褶皱、并不柔软的脑组织 → 大脑的；理智的

root: 拉丁 cerebrum「脑」+ -alis/-al；cerebrum 的更深来源不确定，与希腊 kara「头」的联系仅为假说；它并非英语 brain 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from anatomy to argument: the brain, its cortex, its vessels, intellectual art, mental work, a fixed disease name, the hemispheres, and the brain compared across species.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从解剖走向论辩：脑、皮层、血管、偏重思辨的艺术、脑力工作、固定的疾病名、大脑半球，以及跨物种比较的脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded grey mass under cold light, its creases like a map of thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷光下的一团灰色褶皱，褶纹像一张思考的地图。

branches.en: THE CORTEX AND ITS HALVES: the outer sheet and the two sides.
branches.cn: 皮层与两半球：脑的外层和它的左右两半。

branches.en: CLINICAL PLACES: vessels that bleed, and a fixed disease name.
branches.cn: 临床位置：会出血的血管，以及一个固定的疾病名。

branches.en: MENTAL WORK: tasks that consume attention rather than muscle.
branches.cn: 脑力工作：消耗注意力而非肌肉的任务。

branches.en: ACROSS SPECIES: the same organ measured over evolutionary time.
branches.cn: 跨物种：同一个器官在演化时间中被测量。

branches.en: ONE WORD, TWO WORLDS: the same adjective serves the dissection room and the art review.
branches.cn: 同一个词两个世界：同一个形容词既用于解剖室，也用于艺评。

intro.en: Cerebral is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective ending; the same stem also builds cerebrum, cerebellum and cerebrospinal.
intro.cn: cerebral 是拉丁名词加拉丁形容词词尾；同一词干还构成 cerebrum、cerebellum 与 cerebrospinal。

latinIntro.en: Latin cerebrum brain gives cerebralis and the diminutive cerebellum; cerebrosus described a hot-headed person, showing that the brain stem also carried a temperament sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cerebrum「脑」衍生 cerebralis 与指小形式 cerebellum；cerebrosus 形容脾气急躁的人，说明这个词干也带有性情义。

items.example: Latin anatomy named the organ cerebrum.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学把这个器官称为 cerebrum。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The scan showed a cerebral bleed.
items.exampleCN: 扫描显示脑部出血。

items.example: The cerebellum coordinates balance.
items.exampleCN: 小脑协调平衡。

items.example: Cerebrospinal fluid surrounds the cord.
items.exampleCN: 脑脊液包围脊髓。

items.example: He approached the problem cerebrally.
items.exampleCN: 他以理智的方式处理这个问题。

items.example: The essay is pure cerebration.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章纯粹是思辨。

items.meaning: the outer layer of the brain
items.example: The cerebral cortex handles language.
items.exampleCN: 大脑皮层处理语言。

items.meaning: a movement disorder from early brain damage
items.meaningCN: 由早期脑损伤引起的运动障碍
items.example: Cerebral palsy affects muscle control.
items.exampleCN: 脑瘫影响肌肉控制。
